items.name: TiqNumber — the one formatter
items.purpose: The single locale-driven path every figure in the product passes through, so a number cannot be formatted one way on screen, another in the PDF and a third in Afrikaans.
items.anatomy:
Pure Dart, no BuildContext, so the PDF isolate shares it. Replaces `NumberFormat('#,##0.#','en_US')` in rich_figures.dart (line 14) and every local `toStringAsFixed`.

SEPARATORS — pinned in a table, never inherited from ICU (CLDR's en_ZA has moved across releases and a silent change would re-format every figure in the product). Group separator U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE in BOTH locales, every 3 digits, integer part only, never applied below 10 000: "9999", then "10 000". Decimal separator: en → FULL STOP; af → COMMA. That one glyph is the whole locale difference: en "1 284 990.5", af "1 284 990,5".

MINUS — U+2212 TRUE MINUS, never U+002D hyphen, never brackets, never a trailing CR/DR. It hugs the first digit with no space and sits INSIDE the currency: "−R 1 284,00", not "R −1 284,00".

ZAR — symbol "R" + U+00A0, always leading. Plain money carries exactly 2 decimals. Compact money carries 2 significant decimals ("R 1,28 mln"). Cents are never dropped in a table, an export or a scrub readout.

COMPACT SCALE — pinned, not ICU-derived, and translator-signed: en k / m / bn / tn; af k / mln / mrd / bln. U+00A0 before the scale word. Compaction fires per role, above these glyph counts of the PLAIN rendering: hero.figure 4, hero.figure.compact 5, display 6, figure.l 6, figure.m 8, figure.s 10. Never in a table twin, a scrub readout, an export or a machine identifier.

PRECISION — the client never invents it. The wire carries `value` and `decimals`. Defaults when `decimals` is absent: pct 0, pts 1, money 2, counts 0, rates 1, score 0. Rounding half-away-from-zero. A non-zero magnitude that would round to 0 renders at one more decimal place; if still 0 it renders "<0,1". A count is never given a decimal.

UNITS — 'pct' → "%" appended with NO space, INSIDE the mono run (a column of percentages must align on the sign). 'pts' → " pt"/" pts" as an Onest affix. 'ZAR' → R prefix affix. Bare counts take a word from the caller ("lines", "outlets") as an Onest affix, never a bare number floating in a tile.

FONT SPLIT — the mono run is digits, group separators, the decimal mark, U+2212, U+2014 and "%". Everything else — R, pts, lines, mln, /100 — is an Onest affix in its own slot. Affix sizes, baseline-aligned alphabetic, s1 4dp gap: hero 72→affix 20/600; hero.compact 56→18/600; display 40→16/600; figure.l 32→14/600; figure.m 22→12/600; figure.s 16→11/700. Currency affix ink-2, unit affix ink-3.

SUBSET GUARANTEE — the CI `pyftsubset` step must retain U+2212, U+2014, U+00A0, U+0025, U+003C, U+002E, U+002C and U+0030–0039 in JetBrains Mono, or the whole layer renders tofu. A test asserts each codepoint is present in the shipped TTF. The same test asserts that U+25B2 and U+25BC are NOT referenced anywhere in Dart source — rich_figures.dart lines 56–60 currently build `TileDelta.text` from those two glyphs, which is a live bug the moment the font is subset, and the Delta component replaces that string with a painted triangle.
items.states: Positive: plain. Negative: true minus, magnitude unchanged. Zero: "0" — always rendered, never suppressed, never an em dash, never hidden behind "no data". Null: em dash U+2014 in ink-3 at the figure's own role size and mono face, with the unit affix SUPPRESSED (never "—%") and the eyebrow intact. NaN / infinite: treated as null and logged; a chart skips the point rather than plotting it as zero (existing rule in rich_figures.dart, kept). Delta rounding to zero: rendered unsigned — "−0%" is a movement that did not happen (existing rule, kept). Percentage over 100: rendered as sent; share-of-shelf and attainment legitimately exceed 100.
items.behaviour: Called once per build, no animation of its own. The count-up animator formats at EVERY frame through this same function, so a sweeping figure never shows a different separator convention from its resting state, and the final frame is the exact value, not the tween's float (existing rule in CountUpFigure, kept). Locale comes from `Localizations.localeOf(context)` at the call site and is passed in; the formatter is locale-explicit so the isolate cannot fall back to the host locale.
items.modes: Identical in Night, Day and Veld. Format is not a skin. The only mode effect: Veld never compacts below figure.l — an agent reading a number in the sun gets the whole number, because there is no hover, no tooltip and no second look.
items.accessibility: The screen-reader string is built from the SAME parts but spoken, not glyphed: "minus one million two hundred and eighty-four thousand rand" comes from `NumberFormat` plus the unit word, never from the visual string, because TalkBack reads U+00A0 as a pause and U+2212 as nothing. Every figure widget therefore carries both a visual string and a `semanticsValue`. The em dash is never spoken as "dash": null announces the reason instead ("no visits in this window").
items.amber: None. A formatter has no colour.
items.screenshot: Not a visual. Its test table is two columns of the same twelve numbers, identical except that every decimal mark in the right column is a comma: 1 284 990.5 / 1 284 990,5 · −R 1 284,00 / −R 1 284,00 · R 1.28 mln / R 1,28 mln · 0 / 0 · — / —.

items.name: MotionBudget
items.purpose: One named gate that decides whether anything in this surface moves — added because a dozen components were gating on "battery-saver", which is not a thing Flutter can read, and a promise the code cannot keep is worse than no promise.
items.anatomy:
`MotionBudget` is an `InheritedNotifier` installed once above the app, exposing one boolean: `still`. Every component in this surface reads `MotionBudget.of(context).still` and nothing else. The words "reduce-motion", "battery-saver" and "Veld" are deleted from all twelve components' behaviour fields and live here, once.

`still` is the OR of three inputs, and the spec names exactly what backs each:
1. `MediaQuery.disableAnimations` — real today. On Android it comes from `AccessibilityFeatures.disableAnimations`, which the embedder derives from `Settings.Global.TRANSITION_ANIMATION_SCALE == 0`. It is an accessibility setting, NOT power saving, and the two must never be conflated again.
2. `skin == SkinMode.veld` — real today, read from TiqSkin.
3. `powerSave` — NOT REAL TODAY. Flutter exposes no power API. It requires a named deliverable, listed in the flutter field and costed: an `EventChannel` backed on Android by `PowerManager.isPowerSaveMode` plus a receiver on `ACTION_POWER_SAVE_MODE_CHANGED`, and on iOS by `NSProcessInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled` plus `NSProcessInfoPowerStateDidChangeNotification`. Roughly forty lines per platform.

UNTIL THAT CHANNEL SHIPS, `powerSave` IS `const false`, AND IT SAYS SO AT THE DECLARATION. That is the whole point of putting it here: if the product is lying about honouring power saving, the lie is one line in one file with a TODO and a ticket number on it, not a phrase repeated in twelve component specs where nobody can see that it resolves to nothing.

Battery LEVEL is deliberately not an input. A phone at 9% that the user has not put into power saving has not asked for anything, and changing the composition of a screen because of a reading the user did not act on is the class of behaviour the AmberLedger's retirement rule also forbids.
items.states: still == false → every animation in this surface runs as specified. still == true → every count-up, bar grow, arc sweep, marker travel, stagger, skeleton rule and live pulse is set instantly at its final value; no fades, no enters, no haptic-paired transitions. Transitional: `still` flipping mid-animation cancels the controller and jumps to the end value on the next frame — it never reverses and never eases out, because a motion setting turned on mid-sweep should stop motion, not perform one last one. Unknown (channel not yet installed) → false, as above.
items.behaviour: Read at build, not per frame. The three subscribers to the application's single `Ticker` — the skeleton's travelling rule, the live pulse and the count-up controller pool — each check `still` on subscribe and unsubscribe when it turns true, so a still screen has zero ticker subscribers and the raster thread goes idle. That is the measurable claim: on a 2 GB Android with animations off, this surface schedules no frames at rest.
items.modes: Night and Day consult all three inputs. Veld forces `still` true by construction — `TiqSkin.veld()` cannot be built with motion enabled, the same way it cannot be built with Console density.
items.accessibility: This IS an accessibility mechanism, and it is one-way: every state reachable with motion is reachable without it, because no component in this surface encodes anything in motion alone. The one motion-coded signal in the direction — the amber live pulse — degrades to a filled square plus the word "Live", specified at the AmberLedger, and its slot is retired rather than reassigned.
items.amber: None of its own. It is the reason the live pulse can be amber at all: a signal defined by animation must have a defined still form, and this is where the still form is guaranteed.
items.screenshot: Not a visual. In the debug overlay it is one line: `MotionBudget.still = true (veld)` or `false (a11y:off, veld:off, powerSave:UNIMPLEMENTED #403)`.

items.name: FigureSlot
items.purpose: The atom every number in the product is rendered by: one formatted mono run, an optional affix, a measured fitting rule, and a declared behaviour for null.
items.anatomy:
A `Row(crossAxisAlignment: baseline, textBaseline: alphabetic)` inside a fixed-min-height box, laid out by `LayoutBuilder`.

Slots left to right: [currency affix] [mono run] [unit affix] [provisional marker]. s1 4dp between the mono run and either affix; 0dp before "%", which is inside the run.

FACE — JetBrains Mono Medium 500 for the mono run at figure roles, Bold 700 at hero and display roles, `FontFeature.tabularFigures()` redundant but declared. Onest for affixes at the TiqNumber affix weights.

ROLE SIZES (size/weight/line-height): hero.figure 72/700/0.92; hero.figure.compact 56/700/0.95; display 40/700/1.00; figure.l 32/500/1.05; figure.m 22/500/1.10; figure.s 16/500/1.20. Tracking 0 at every role — the direction's −2.5% was an Archivo instruction and negative tracking collapses monospace cells into each other.

THE FITTING RULE — MEASURED, INCLUDING THE PARTS THE FIRST DRAFT DID NOT MEASURE.
The first draft's formula was `glyphs × 0.6 × size × textScaler`, and it was wrong twice. (a) It measured only the mono run, while the currency and unit affixes are proportional Onest sitting in the same Row, plus up to two 4dp gaps: an "R 1 284 990,50" hero passed the check on twelve mono glyphs at 56dp and then overflowed by ~20dp on the 18dp "R" and its gap. (b) `textScaler` is not a scalar. On Android 14+ `MediaQuery.textScalerOf` returns a non-linear `TextScaler` that compresses large sizes and expands small ones, so multiplying by a factor mis-picks the role in both directions at the system's largest setting.

The rule is therefore: for each candidate role, from largest down — scale the role's size with `MediaQuery.textScalerOf(context).scale(size)`, compute the mono run as `glyphs × 0.600 em × scaledSize`, measure EACH affix with a `TextPainter` at its own scaled size in the same pass, add the 4dp gaps, and accept the first role whose total ≤ (slot width − 8dp). Floor at figure.m 22.

Below the floor, DO NOT use `FittedBox`. `RenderFittedBox` extends `RenderProxyBox` and reports its child's baseline unscaled by the fitted transform, so the moment `scaleDown` engages inside a baseline Row the Onest affixes align to a baseline the shrunken digits are no longer on — the "R" floats roughly 12dp above its own number. Instead, compute the fitted ratio and pass the reduced size to `TextStyle.fontSize`, scaling every affix size and the 4dp gaps by the SAME ratio, so the slot shrinks as one object with a real baseline. Hard floor 18dp; below that the layout is wrong, not the number.

The published glyph-count table (≤3 → 72, 4–6 → 56, 7–8 → 40, 9–11 → 32, 12+ → compact first) is DOCUMENTATION OF THE EXPECTED OUTCOME at 360dp, 1.0×, Latin digits, no affix. It is not the mechanism and no code reads it.

COLOUR — mono run ink-1 (Night #EEE9DF: 15.77:1 on ground, 12.67:1 on surface, 11.12:1 on raised; Day #1B2632: 12.67:1 on Palladian, 14.34:1 on card; Veld #0E141A: 18.52:1 on white). Affixes ink-3 / ink-2 per TiqNumber. Never a severity hue: a figure is a quantity, and its verdict lives in the delta, the band word or the bar.
items.states: Default. Null → em dash in ink-3, affixes suppressed, slot height unchanged so a grid never reflows the day a figure goes missing. Loading → a static well-fill block at the exact rendered width of a representative figure for that role, radius 6. Provisional → 2dp dotted ink-3 underline 4dp below the mono run's baseline box. Live → a 6dp dot before the eyebrow, never on the figure. Error → em dash plus the cluster's error footer; the slot never turns red. Pressed → not interactive on its own; inherits the row or tile that owns it. Counting → see behaviour: the slot is width-reserved for the duration. Over-wide at the 18dp floor → the run middle-truncates with a horizontal ellipsis and the whole slot becomes tappable, opening the table twin at that row.
items.behaviour:
COUNT-UP RESERVES ITS OWN WIDTH. With tabular figures the glyph count changes during a sweep — 0→71 crosses one advance to two, 99→100 crosses two to three — and at 72dp one JetBrains Mono advance is 43dp. Unreserved, the "/100" affix, the severity glyph and the band word sit 43dp left of their landing place for the first quarter-second of the most important moment in an agent's day, then slide right. So for the animation's duration the slot is a `SizedBox` at `max(glyphs(from), glyphs(to)) × advance × scaledSize`, padded on the LEFT so the run stays right-aligned against its affixes and the affixes never move; it releases to the true width on the final frame. Goldens at 9→10 and 0→100, captured mid-frame.

Count-up is 600ms ease-out-quart, one `AnimationController` per visible cluster, never one per slot, and it runs ONLY on a final value that has just arrived — a provisional value is set instantly, because a sweeping number is the gesture of arrival. `MotionBudget.still` sets everything instantly. The role is re-measured on `didChangeDependencies` when the `TextScaler` changes, so rotating or changing font size re-picks the role rather than shrinking one that no longer fits. Slow data: the skeleton block holds 600ms before an Oatmeal 2px rule begins travelling its top edge at 1400ms linear — never amber, because a skeleton is loading and not live.
items.modes: Night: ink-1 on ground/surface/raised at 15.77 / 12.67 / 11.12:1. Day: ink-1 #1B2632 at 12.67:1 on Palladian, 14.34:1 on card. Veld: veld-ink #0E141A at 18.52:1; role sizes step figure.s 16→18, figure.m 22→24, figure.l 32→34, display 40→42, hero unchanged; the weight floor of 600 moves figure.l and below from Medium to Bold; the skin's +0.5% tracking does NOT apply to mono; the +0.05 line-height does.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(value: <spoken form>, label: <the eyebrow or row name>)`. The visual glyph string is `excludeSemantics`-d so TalkBack never reads U+00A0 as a pause or drops U+2212. At 2.0× the role steps down by measurement rather than clipping; the slot's min-height is `roleLineHeight × 2.0` so a grid does not jump when one tile scales and another does not. Tap target: none of its own; the owning row provides ≥44dp (Field 48, Veld 56). Non-colour encoding: the figure is the value — no colour carries meaning here at all.
items.amber: None, ever. Amber is emitted light; a digit is a reading. The hero delta on the manager dashboard was amber in an earlier draft and is now `bad` — a severity-coded figure has no amber in it.
items.screenshot: A left-aligned number on near-black: 61 in warm off-white monospace at 32dp, a small ink-3 % hard against the last digit, nothing else in the box. Beside it in the null case, an em dash the same height sitting exactly where the 6 was, the % gone.

items.name: Delta
items.purpose: The optional slot beside a figure that says which way it moved, whether that is good news, and whether the comparison is worth making at all — the pill's wash deleted, the shape kept.
items.anatomy:
An inline `Row` on the figure's baseline, 8dp below it when the figure is hero or display, beside it at figure.l and under.

Slots: [8dp triangle] s1 4dp [signed magnitude, figure.s 16/500 mono at figure.l and above, label 13/500 mono below] s2 8dp [comparedTo, meta 12 ink-3, wrapping].

THE TRIANGLE IS DRAWN, NOT TYPED — a `CustomPaint` path, 8dp base × 7dp height, flat-bottomed pointing up, flat-topped pointing down. ▲/▼ as glyphs are banned: their vertical metrics differ per face and they are absent from a subset font. This is not hypothetical — `TileDelta.text` in rich_figures.dart lines 56–60 builds exactly those two characters today, and the pyftsubset step this surface specifies would render them as tofu. That getter is deleted with this component.  Flat: an 8×2dp rectangle, not a triangle, not a dash.

COLOUR — triangle and magnitude take the SENTIMENT colour, which the server sends and the client never infers: good (Night #6FE0AE, 11.76:1 on ground, 8.30:1 on raised; Day #14664A 5.73:1 on Palladian; Veld #0F5039 9.43:1 on white), bad (Night #FF7D8C 7.78 / 5.49; Day #8C1B2C 7.52:1; Veld #7A0F22 10.94:1), neutral (ink-3). DIRECTION comes from the server's `up` field and is the triangle; VERDICT comes from `sentiment` and is the colour. A stock-out count going up is bad and a spoilage count going down is good, so neither is derived from the other — the existing contract in `TileDelta.tryParse`, kept intact.

NO WASH, NO PILL, NO BORDER, NO RADIUS. `DeltaChip` (14%-alpha wash, radius 999) and `DeltaPill` (fixed status washes) are both deleted. The reason, stated so it is not re-litigated: a coloured wash behind an 11px figure is a second severity fill competing with the severity system's own two commitment levels, and at 14% alpha on a 6-bit LCD at 40% backlight it is one quantisation level — invisible where it matters and noisy where it does not.
items.states: Rise / fall / flat as above. No baseline (`pct: null` because the prior period was zero): the words "up from none", triangle up, no percentage, sentiment as sent — never "n/a" beside a triangle, never ∞. Rounds to zero: unsigned magnitude and the flat rectangle, with the word "No change" replacing the magnitude at figure.l and above. Suppressed — CURRENT window below threshold: the delta slot is REMOVED (not greyed) and replaced by the meta line "too few visits to compare". Suppressed — BASELINE window below threshold: THE SAME REMOVAL, and this is the fix for the failure the low-sample rule missed entirely. A delta compares two windows and each has its own n. Gauteng North loses week 37 to a strike, gets one visit at 100%, then twenty visits at 84% in week 38; the first draft rendered 84% in full ink-1 with a solid red triangle and "−16 pts vs week 37", a hard verdict computed against a single visit, and a manager reassigns an agent over it. The wire therefore carries `baselineSampleSize` beside `sampleSize`, the same thresholds apply to it, and below threshold the meta line reads "last week had only 1 visit — not compared." On a load-shedding calendar this is the common case, not the edge case. Null figure: no delta slot at all — ticket #392's rule, never an arrow next to nothing. Reconciliation delta: neutral ink-3 always, never good/bad, triangle hollow at 1.5dp stroke. Loading: absent; the slot does not skeleton, because a tile that will have no delta must not promise one. Pressed: inherits its row.
items.behaviour: No motion of its own; it fades in with its tile's 200ms enter at the end of the 40ms stagger, AFTER the count-up has settled, so the verdict never appears beside a number still sweeping. On a manager tile it is tappable at the owning tile's target and opens the comparison-window picker. Absent or slow sentiment: renders neutral, never guesses. `MotionBudget.still`: appears with its tile, no fade.
items.modes: Night / Day / Veld per the colour list. Veld: triangle 10dp base × 9dp height, magnitude at label 16/600, and the DIRECTION WORD ("up", "down") is spelled out beside it, because at a 9:1 contrast floor there is no room for a hue distinction to do the work; good/bad become the solid Veld blocks only when the delta is the row's severity carrier, which it normally is not.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(label: 'Down 19 points against last week, which is bad')` — direction word, magnitude with unit, baseline, verdict word, in that order, and where a baseline is weak, "last week had only 1 visit, not compared" instead of a number. The verdict word is always in the string, so colour is never the only carrier. At 2.0× the row wraps: triangle and magnitude on line one, `comparedTo` on line two. Tap target inherits the tile's 44/48/56dp.
items.amber: None. This is the single most tempting place in the product to use amber for "watch" and it is explicitly banned: severity abandons amber's hue band entirely, and a caret on a severity-coded delta was a named error in the direction.
items.screenshot: Under a big off-white 61, a small solid mint triangle pointing up, then +4 pts in mono mint, then in dim grey "vs week 37". In the bad case the identical arrangement, triangle down, in a soft red. In the suppressed case no triangle at all — only the grey words last week had only 1 visit — not compared.

items.name: StatTile
items.purpose: One figure in an instrument cluster — eyebrow, figure, optional meter, optional delta — with no card of its own, laid out first for the phone it will actually be read on.
items.anatomy:
No card, no border, no shadow, no radius. A cell separated from its neighbours by 1px hairlines, not by gaps. Padding s4 16dp (Field s5 20dp, Veld s6 24dp).

THE PHONE LAYOUT IS THE PRIMARY LAYOUT, and the first draft did not have one. At 360dp with a 20dp Console gutter and 16dp panel padding the inner panel is 288dp, below the 320dp threshold at which the cluster would go 2×2 — so the square cell the first draft specified, and every argument built on a "2×2 grid of tiles", describes a screen no manager holds. The phone tile is HORIZONTAL:

Row 1, a baseline `Row`: [eyebrow 11/700/+8% uppercase ink-2, `Expanded`, wrapping to 3 lines] s3 12dp [FigureSlot figure.l 32, right-aligned]. The figures of a stacked cluster therefore align on one right edge, which is the instrument-panel read and the reason the run is monospace.
Row 2, at s2 8dp: the Meter, full tile width, 3dp.
Row 3, at s2 8dp: the Delta, left-aligned, with the sample meta wrapping beside it.

Height 88dp at 1.0× with a one-line eyebrow and no meter, ~112dp with both, against the ~143dp the vertical cell cost — about 160dp of fold returned across four tiles. Field 96dp, Veld 128dp. At 2.0× with a two-line Afrikaans eyebrow ("BESKIKBAARHEID OP RAK") the tile lands near 150dp rather than 230dp.

The VERTICAL cell — eyebrow, figure, meter, delta stacked — is the CONSOLE layout, ≥320dp of inner panel width, which means tablet and desktop. Min height 96dp there. Every screenshot in this surface that shows a 2×2 grid is a Console screenshot and is labelled as one.

The hairline is `hairline-decorative` (Night #3A4B60, 1.72:1 on surface; Day #DED7C9) and is explicitly exempt from 3:1 because it is never the sole cue that two regions differ — the uppercase kicker and the 16dp padding do that. In Veld it becomes a 2px #1B2632 solid rule.

The eyebrow is one of only two surviving uses of the uppercase kicker in the whole system (the other is the plate's), which is what earns it.
items.states: Default. No data → its own item. Low sample → its own item. Provisional → its own item. Loading → the eyebrow renders immediately (the label is known before the value is), the figure becomes a well-fill block at a representative width, the meter track draws with no fill, the delta is absent; after 600ms the cluster's shared Oatmeal rule travels. Error → eyebrow, em dash, and a meta line "Couldn't load" with a 7dp half-filled `bad` triangle; the retry lives once in the cluster footer, never per tile. Offline/stale → the cached figure renders at full ink and the cluster footer carries the held chip; dimming a stale number would be a lie about its accuracy. Live → a 6dp dot before the eyebrow, per AmberLedger. Pressed → the tile takes a `lifted` fill (Night #2C3B4D, Day #F4F0E8, Veld a 2px #1B2632 inset ring) for 120ms and scales to 0.98. Disabled → does not exist; a tile is either a figure or an absence.
items.behaviour: Tap opens the figure's provenance: the window, the sample size, the definition, a link to the table twin. A composite number nobody can decompose is a number you cannot act on. Long-press copies the figure in plain, uncompacted, locale-correct form. Count-up 600ms on the arrival of a final value only; the tiles in a cluster share one controller and land inside 320ms at a 40ms stagger. `MotionBudget.still`: instant. Data slow → the skeleton above. Data absent → the no-data state, never a zero. Data wrong-typed → skipped by `StatTileData.listFrom` (existing behaviour) and the cluster reflows to the tiles it can read.
items.modes: Night: no fill at all — the panel's `surface` #1B2632 shows through; ink-1 figure, ink-2 eyebrow at 8.57:1, ink-3 meta at 5.78:1. Day: the panel's #FAF7F2, ink-2 at 9.04:1. Veld: white, 2px #1B2632 rules, every type role stepped, min height 128dp, and a maximum of TWO tiles per cluster — Veld halves density, and four figures is analysis, which nobody does outdoors.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(container: true, label: eyebrow, value: spoken figure, hint: 'Double tap for how this is measured')`. Announcement order is eyebrow, figure, delta-with-verdict, sample. Tap target: the full tile, ≥88dp tall. At 2.0× the eyebrow takes its lines, the figure re-picks its role by measurement, the meter and delta keep their rows, and the tile grows — nothing is pinned and nothing clips. Non-colour: every distinction in the tile is a word or a shape.
items.amber: None. Not in the figure, not in the eyebrow, not in the meter's target tick — see Meter, where the override is re-argued against the phone layout rather than the imaginary grid.
items.screenshot: On a phone: a dark navy panel holding four full-width rows divided by faint hairlines. Each row has small-caps oatmeal type at the left — OUT-OF-STOCK LINES — and a big off-white monospace figure hard against the right edge, all four figures aligned on one column. Beneath each, a thin full-width track with a short fill and a pale tick standing proud of it, and under that a small red triangle, +12, and in grey, vs week 37.

items.name: StatTile · no data
items.purpose: The state the product currently fakes with a zero, and the one ticket #392 exists for: the window contained nothing to measure.
items.anatomy: Eyebrow unchanged, full opacity, ink-2 — the label is still true. Figure replaced by U+2014 EM DASH in mono at figure.l 32, ink-3 (Night #A79E8C: 7.19:1 on ground, 5.78:1 on surface, 5.07:1 on raised; Day #676052: 5.15:1 on Palladian, 5.83:1 on card; Veld #4A4437 9.66:1). Unit affix suppressed. Meter: the track renders at 3dp with NO fill, NO target tick, AND its 1px `edge-structure` outline (see Meter) — an empty track needs an edge or it is invisible against the panel. Delta slot: absent, not greyed. Below, at s2 8dp, one meta 12/400 ink-3 line naming the absence in the window's own words: "No visits in this window" / "Geen besoeke in hierdie venster nie". Where the server knows the cause, the cause replaces the generic line: "No competitor on shelf", "Outlet closed all week".
items.states: Generic absence (no visits). Caused absence (the server names it). Filtered absence — the window has data but the filter excludes it: same em dash, different line, "No outlets match this filter", plus a ghost `Clear filter` in the cluster footer. Partial absence — the metric exists but this dimension of it does not: handled by the dimension breakdown's hatch, not here. Never: a zero, a 0%, a "—%", a delta arrow, a 0-length bar, or the tile being hidden. Hiding is worse than the em dash: a cluster that silently drops a tile changes shape and the manager cannot tell whether the metric was bad or missing.
items.behaviour: No count-up — there is nothing to count to. No stagger delay; a no-data tile lands with the others on the first frame it is known, so the cluster does not appear to be still loading. Tap is still live and opens the same provenance sheet, which leads with why there is no figure and what would produce one ("3 visits are scheduled for this outlet this week"). Long-press: nothing to copy; the haptic is suppressed rather than firing on an empty clipboard.
items.modes: Identical structure in all three. Night and Day: em dash ink-3. Veld: em dash at figure.l 34/600 in veld-ink-2 #4A4437 at 9.66:1, meta stepped 12→14, and Veld never abbreviates the reason — there is no tap-to-find-out outdoors.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(value: 'No data', hint: 'No visits in this window')` — the em dash is never spoken as "dash" or "em dash", which is what an unlabelled `Text('—')` produces today. The reason is part of the same utterance, so a screen-reader user gets absence and cause together. At 2.0× the reason wraps to as many lines as it needs and the tile grows.
items.amber: None.
items.screenshot: A row the same height as its three neighbours, but where their monospace figures sit against the right edge, a single long grey dash, and beneath it in smaller grey type, No visits in this window. The small-caps label at the left is as bright as every other label on the panel.

items.name: StatTile · low sample
items.purpose: A figure that is arithmetically true and epistemically weak — a 100% OSA from one visit — marked so a manager does not act on it.
items.anatomy: Thresholds declared in the theme, not per-caller: rates and percentages need n ≥ 5; averages need n ≥ 3; a score needs n ≥ 1 (a single visit's score is a fact about that visit, not an estimate). Below threshold the figure renders at its normal role and size but in ink-2 rather than ink-1 — one register down, the same step the system uses for secondary text everywhere, so it reads as less committed without reading as disabled. A 7dp hollow square glyph (1.5dp stroke, ink-3) sits s1 4dp before the meta line. Meta line 12/400 ink-3: "from 3 visits". The delta slot is removed and replaced by "too few visits to compare" — and separately removed when the BASELINE window is thin, which is the more dangerous case and is specified at Delta. The meter, if present, draws its fill as a 1.5dp OUTLINE rather than a solid: outline-versus-fill is a shape distinction that survives greyscale, sun and deuteranopia, which an alpha reduction does not.
items.states: Below threshold with a known n (the normal case). Below threshold with unknown n — no `sampleSize` on the wire: the figure still steps to ink-2 and the meta reads "small sample", never a number the client invented. Exactly at threshold: normal treatment, no marker; the boundary is not a gradient. Zero sample: not low sample — the no-data state takes over. Low sample AND provisional: both markers render; the dotted underline and the hollow square are different channels and do not collide. Current window fine, baseline thin: the figure is NOT stepped down — it is a good figure — only the delta is removed, with its own sentence.
items.behaviour: No count-up: a weak figure does not get the arrival gesture. Tap opens the provenance sheet, leading with the sample and the threshold ("5 visits needed for a reliable rate; this window has 3"). In a ranked bar list the same rule draws the row's bar as an outline and appends "n=3" in mono meta after the value; in a trend chart a low-sample bucket is a 4dp hollow circle with the segments either side dashed 3-3, so a thin stretch of the series is visibly thin rather than silently equal.
items.modes: Night ink-2 #C9C1B1 (8.57:1 on surface, 9.51:1 on the well). Day ink-2 #4A4437 (9.04:1 on card). Veld: there is no ink step available under a 9:1 floor, so Veld carries low sample by WORDS ONLY — the figure stays veld-ink and the meta reads "Only 3 visits — treat as rough" at 14/600. That is the honest answer: Veld's contrast floor removes the register, so the register is replaced by language rather than faked with a hue.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(value: '100 percent', hint: 'From 3 visits, below the 5 needed for a reliable rate')`. The hollow square has no semantic of its own; the hint carries it. Colour is not the signal in any mode — "from 3 visits" is always present. At 2.0× the meta wraps and the tile grows.
items.amber: None. Low confidence is exactly the thing a designer reaches for amber to say, and exactly what the amber law forbids: amber tells you where to look, never how much to trust.
items.screenshot: A row whose figure is a shade dimmer than the row above it — warm oatmeal rather than bright bone — with a small hollow square and the words from 3 visits under it, and where its neighbour has a red triangle and a percentage, only the grey words too few visits to compare.

items.name: StatCluster
items.purpose: The instrument panel that holds the tiles: the only place in the product where several figures sit together, and the thing that owns their shared controller, their shared footer and their share of the amber ledger.
items.anatomy:
Lives inside one Panel (Night: `surface` #1B2632, radius 14, 1px `edge-structure` #5A7088 at exactly 3.00:1 on the surface, no shadow, padding s4 16dp. Day: #FAF7F2, radius 14, 1px #857C6B at 3.86:1, sh1. Veld: white, radius 0, 2px #1B2632).

The Palladian@10% top rim survives, and its measured contrast is 1.32:1 — one quantisation level on the target panel. It stays only because it encodes NOTHING: it is a light-source cue in a direction whose whole thesis is light, and if a given screen cannot resolve it, nothing is lost. That is precisely the test `DeltaChip`'s 14% wash failed, because that wash carried severity. A decoration may be invisible; an encoding may not.

LAYOUT. Phone (inner width < 320dp, which is every phone): a single column of horizontal tiles, divided by full-bleed 1px hairlines, no vertical divider. Console (≥320dp inner): the 2×2 grid of vertical cells. The threshold is measured by `LayoutBuilder` on inner panel width, never guessed from textScale.

COUNT. Phone: at most 4 tiles, and 3 is the recommended figure — the fourth is the one a manager least often acts on and it belongs in the table twin. Four horizontal tiles plus a footer is about 470dp, which is most of a phone's fold before the ranked bars are reached, and that is a cost the route should pay deliberately rather than by default. Console: up to 6 in a 2-column grid; beyond that the server is asked for a table, not a cluster.

Footer, when it has anything to say: a full-width 1px hairline, s3 12dp, then a `Wrap` holding [held chip] [source line] [retry ghost] [See the numbers]. "See the numbers" is mandatory whenever the cluster is accompanied by any chart. Held chip: Oatmeal ink on the `well` (#141D27 Night, 9.51:1; #E2DBCC Day, 7.01:1), 1px `edge-control` (#7C93AC at 5.37:1 on the Night well; #6E6657 at 4.12:1 on the Day well — `edge-structure` is not used on the Day well, where it measures 2.99:1), radius 6, height 44 (Field 48, Veld 56), a 7dp filled SQUARE glyph, label "Held · as at 14:02" — deliberately not a severity, because queued work is the normal state of South African field connectivity.
items.states: Complete. Mixed (some tiles no-data) — the column does not reflow; absent figures are em dashes in place. All no-data → the whole cluster collapses to one left-aligned empty state inside the panel: a 40dp 2px-stroke line drawing in `edge-control` (6.02:1 on ground), a title.m headline, one body line, one ghost button; never four em dashes, which reads as a broken screen rather than an empty window. Loading → all tiles skeleton simultaneously (never one at a time, which reads as a stall); ONE shared 1400ms Oatmeal rule travels the whole cluster's top edge. Error → the tiles show their error state and ONE `Retry` ghost appears in the footer. Offline → cached values, held chip. Partial error → the tiles that loaded render normally; the footer reads "2 of 4 figures couldn't load" with one retry. Console odd count → 3 tiles in a 2×2 leaves the fourth cell empty with no hairlines drawn into it, never a stretched third tile.
items.behaviour: One `AnimationController` drives every count-up in the cluster. One 40ms stagger, capped so the last tile starts no later than 240ms. Tiles enter over 200ms. On refresh the figures re-count from their PREVIOUS value, not from zero — counting down from 61 to 48 is the truthful gesture; sweeping up from zero again would imply a fresh measurement. `MotionBudget.still`: instant. No blur, no shadow and no gradient inside the cluster, per the list budget.
items.modes: Night / Day per the Panel spec. Veld: maximum 2 tiles, stacked, separated by 2px rules, no footer chips beyond the held chip and See the numbers, both at 56dp.
items.accessibility: The Panel is a `Semantics(container: true)` labelled with what the cluster is about ("Four figures for Gauteng North, week 38"). Reading order is visual order and is asserted by a test — a column of Rows reads correctly; a Wrap does not. At 2.0× the phone column simply grows; the Console grid trips its threshold and becomes a column, which is the correct behaviour and not a fallback. Every footer control is ≥44dp.
items.amber: None in the cluster itself. The cluster is where the route's amber slot set is READ, and it holds the budget for its children — but it emits nothing of its own.
items.screenshot: A softly outlined dark panel with a faint lit line along its top edge, holding a single column of four figure rows divided by hairlines, their monospace numbers aligned on one right-hand column. A thin rule at the bottom, and beneath it a small oatmeal chip reading Held · as at 14:02 and a quiet text button, See the numbers.

items.name: Meter
items.purpose: The 3dp bar under a figure that says where the figure sits against its own range or its target — and the progress-to-reward bar ticket #391 asks for, which is the same object at a different height.
items.anatomy:
Track: full width of its tile, height 3dp (Field 4dp, Veld 6dp), radius 2 (Veld 0), fill `lifted` #2C3B4D in Night, `well` #E2DBCC in Day, white with a 2px #1B2632 border in Veld.

Fill: from the left origin, `chart-neutral`. **The neutral has moved**: Night #8B8271 → **#A39887**, Day #676052 → **#5C5648**. The old Night value measured exactly 3.01:1 against its track — the product's most-drawn graphic sitting on the AA floor with 0.01 of margin, which on a 6-bit panel at 40% backlight is a smudge. #A39887 measures 4.02:1 on the track, 5.40:1 on the surface, 6.72:1 on the ground. I did not take it to 4.5:1 as asked, because 4.5 is the threshold for TEXT and a bar is a graphical object at 3:1 — what was wrong was the margin, not the threshold, and 4.02 is a third of a stop of real headroom rather than a rounding error. The Day neutral moves for a second reason: #676052 was byte-identical to Day ink-3, so a bar and a meta line were the same token by accident. #5C5648 measures 5.29:1 on the Day track and is now distinct. In Night, chart-neutral and ink-3 land at the same luminance deliberately — a quiet mark and quiet type belong in the same register.

Minimum rendered fill 2dp so a non-zero value is never invisible; a true zero renders NO fill and the figure above carries it.

THE EMPTY TRACK GETS AN EDGE. The track is only 1.3:1 from the panel behind it, which is fine while a fill sits on it and useless when one does not. So in the zero, null, loading and hatched states — and only then — the track draws a 1px `edge-structure` outline (3.00:1 on the Night surface, 3.86:1 on the Day card). In the filled state there is no outline and no extra draw.

TARGET TICK: 2dp wide, running the full track height and BREAKING the track's top edge by 2dp so it has a silhouette above the bar — a tick that is only a hue change disappears in greyscale. Colour ink-1 (Night #EEE9DF, Day #1B2632, Veld #0E141A). **This remains a deliberate deviation from the direction, which specifies a #FFB162 tick — but the first draft defended it with arithmetic about a 2×2 grid that no phone renders, so here is the real argument.** The ledger counts amber per ROUTE, not per viewport, because a slot that released on scroll would make amber blink in and out as a manager thumbs down a page. A phone dashboard route carries up to four metered tiles and a dimension breakdown carries six, all on the same route, and the dashboard's two slots are already spent on the plate's strip light and the nav underbar. So the tick is ink-1 not because four of them are on screen at once but because up to ten of them are on the route and the route's budget is zero. The silhouette does the work the amber was there to do. Recorded in Open questions.

PROGRESS-TO-REWARD variant: height 10dp (Veld 14dp), radius 5, milestone ticks at each threshold as 2dp ink-1 marks breaking BOTH edges by 2dp, each labelled beneath at meta 12 ink-3 with its reward in words. The fill is `good` (#6FE0AE / #14664A / #0F5039) once the first milestone is cleared and `chart-neutral` before it — a step, not a gradient, so the moment of clearing is perceptible.
items.states: Default fill. Zero → no fill, outlined track only. Over-target → the fill continues past the tick to the track's end and a 2dp ink-1 cap closes it; the value never overflows the track, and "over target" is said in the delta or the word beside it. Over-range → the track's right end takes a 3-notch sawtooth cut and the figure above is authoritative. Null → outlined track, no tick. Low sample → the fill draws as a 1.5dp outline instead of a solid. Loading → outlined track, no fill, no tick. Unknown target → no tick rendered, never a tick at 100 or at the midpoint. Milestone variant, none cleared → neutral fill, all ticks ink-1. Milestone variant, all cleared → full `good` fill and the final tick becomes a 7dp filled circle.
items.behaviour: Grows from the left origin over 320ms, starting after the tile's figure has begun counting — the bar and the number must not arrive at different values at the same instant. Staggers with the tile. `MotionBudget.still`: instant. Refresh animates from the previous fraction, not from zero. Not interactive; the tile owns the tap. In a `ListView` the meter is a plain `DecoratedBox` with no gradient, so it costs nothing per row.
items.modes: Night / Day / Veld per the token list. Veld: 6dp track with a 2px border, fill in veld-ink-2 #4A4437 (9.66:1 on white), tick in veld-ink 2px breaking the top edge by 3dp, and the numeric value ALWAYS printed at the track's right end at figure.s 18 — outdoors the bar is a picture and the number is the reading.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(value: '61 out of 100, target 80')` — the target is in the value string, so the tick's silhouette is reinforced, not relied on. `ExcludeSemantics` when its tile already announces the same figure, to avoid a double read. At 2.0× the meter's height does NOT scale (it is a graphic) but its labels do, and milestone labels stack and wrap. Non-colour: fill length, tick silhouette, printed value.
items.amber: None, including the target tick, against the written direction, for the route-budget reason given in Anatomy. The one amber a meter could hold is a ledger-granted focus, and no meter ever requests a slot.
items.screenshot: Beneath a monospace figure, a hairline-thin dark track with a warm-grey fill running about two thirds across it, and standing proud of the track's top edge a short pale vertical tick at the 80 mark, casting no colour at all. In the empty case the same track with a faint outline all round it and nothing inside.

items.name: RankedBarRow
items.purpose: One row of the ranking: a name, a track, a fill, a value — the atom that has to survive greyscale, deuteranopia, sunlight and a 40-character Afrikaans outlet name.
items.anatomy:
Row height 44dp (Field 48, Veld 64), vertical padding s2 8dp, no divider between rows — the 7dp gap and the track alignment do that.

One line at ≥360dp: [label, flexible, min 92dp, max 40% of row width] s3 12dp [track, expanded] s3 12dp [value, fixed 64dp, right-aligned].

Label: body 15/400 (Console 14) ink-1, MIDDLE-truncated — "Shoprite Kli…Mall" — because the branch is the identifying half and a tail ellipsis destroys it. The focus row's label is body.strong 600.

Track: 6dp, radius 3, `lifted` #2C3B4D (Night), `well` #E2DBCC (Day), white with a 2px #1B2632 border (Veld), with the same empty-state outline rule as the Meter.

Fill: 6dp, radius 3, minimum 2dp. Non-focus `chart-neutral` #A39887 at 4.02:1 on the Night track, #5C5648 at 5.29:1 on the Day track, #4A4437 in Veld.

FOCUS ROW — four channels, never one: (1) fill `flame-600` #FFB162 at 6.37:1 on the Night track, (2) a 12dp `LinearGradient` bloom beneath the bar, stops #FFF1DE@0.55 → #FFB162@0.30 → transparent, painted inside the same draw call — never a `BoxShadow`, never a blur, (3) a filled triangle marker at the bar's origin, 7dp, pointing right, in the fill colour, and (4) the label at body.strong. Hue alone gives 2.12:1 true, 2.11 greyscale, 2.21 deuteranopia, 1.93 protanopia — which is why there are four.

AMBER HERE IS NOW RARE, NOT ROUTINE. Under the revised ledger there is ONE content amber object anywhere in the product, on the answered phase of the Ask TradeIQ route, and this is its first claimant. Everywhere else — the dashboard, every agent screen, every Day and every Veld screen — the focus channel is ink-1 fill at 9.43:1 on the Night track and 11.12:1 on the Day track, plus the marker, plus the weight. The fallback is the HIGHER-contrast option of the two, measured in the same mode (9.43 ink-1 versus 6.37 amber, both on the Night track); the first draft compared a Day number against a Night one and the comparison was meaningless.

Value: mono figure.s 16/500, right-aligned, size-fitted inside its 64dp so a long count reads whole rather than clipping. Focus row's value at 600.
items.states: Default. Focus. Zero → a 2dp stub at the origin plus the value "0"; never a zero-length bar, which is indistinguishable from a missing row. Negative → diverging mode, see the list. Null value → the row is not drawn; a ranking of things that could not be measured is not a ranking. Low sample → fill drawn as a 1.5dp outline, value suffixed " n=3". Tie → identical bar lengths and the server's order preserved without a tie-break marker; ties are real and inventing an order would be worse. Pressed → a `lifted` fill across the full row for 120ms, scale 0.99. Long label at 2.0× → the label takes two lines and the row grows; the track keeps its height and its right-hand alignment. Below 300dp of row width → the row stacks: label on line one, track and value on line two, focus marker to the label's left.
items.behaviour: Grows from the origin over 320ms with a 40ms stagger by index, capped at 8 rows so the last bar starts at 280ms. `MotionBudget.still`: instant. Tap opens that outlet or agent; the whole row is the target, ≥44dp. Long-press copies "name, value". On a pointer the row takes the `lifted` fill.
items.modes: Night: neutral #A39887, focus amber + bloom + marker + weight only when the ledger grants it, otherwise ink-1 + marker + weight. Day: neutral #5C5648, focus #1B2632 + marker + weight, NO bloom — a bloom on paper is a smudge. Veld: neutral #4A4437, focus #0E141A + a 10dp marker + weight, track white with a 2px border, no bloom, no gradient, row 64dp, label 17/600, value 18/600.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(label: 'Shoprite Klipfontein Mall', value: '34 percent', hint: 'Worst in this ranking')` — the focus row's hint states WHY it is focused, so the bloom, the marker and the weight are reinforced by language. Rank position is announced ("1 of 8"). At 2.0× the row grows or stacks; nothing clips. Tap target 44/48/56dp. Non-colour: bar length, marker, weight, printed value, announced rank.
items.amber: At most one in the whole product, and only on the answered phase of the answer route, and only when the ledger grants it — the fill, bloom and origin marker counted as ONE contiguous emitter. Denied, or in Day or Veld, the ink-1 channel is not a degradation: it is the higher-contrast rendering and it is what the great majority of screens will actually ship.
items.screenshot: A row on near-black: an outlet name in off-white at the left, then a dark rounded track across the middle carrying a warm-grey bar about a third of the way, then 34% in monospace at the right. On the answer screen the top row's bar is a warm amber that seems to glow softly onto the track beneath it, with a small amber triangle tucked at its left end and its name set heavier. On the dashboard that same top row is bone white instead, and reads brighter.

items.name: RankedBarList
items.purpose: The worst-first ranking the answer's sentence is about — the shape that turns 'which outlets are failing' into five rows a manager can act on.
items.anatomy:
Sits inside the Panel, under a 1px hairline, never in a card of its own. Header: title.m 16/600 ink-1, subtitle (`comparedTo`) at meta 12 ink-3, s3 12dp, then rows at 7dp intervals.

ORDER IS THE SERVER'S. Worst-first, and what "worst" means depends on the metric — highest-first for a bad-when-up count, lowest-first for a rate. The client neither re-sorts nor second-guesses by magnitude (existing contract in `RankedBarsData.leaderIndex`, kept). The FOCUS is item 0, always, which is why truncation can never hide it.

SCALE: every bar against `maxAbs`. No axis, no gridlines — a ranked list is a comparison of lengths, and a gridline behind five bars is chrome.

CAP: 8 rows, then a 9th row in body ink-2 reading "12 more outlets" with a chevron, opening the table twin. A ranking is an argument, not a database.

FOOTER: the legend when diverging or when a comparison series is present; "See the numbers" always.

PAINT BUDGET, restated so the diverging state cannot break it: no gradient DECORATIONS in a builder row. Rows are `ColoredBox` plus a 1px divider. Hatches are lines in the row's `CustomPainter`, not `BoxDecoration` gradients. The focus row's bloom is the single gradient decoration in the list and it is granted, counted and non-scrolling-critical.
items.states: Normal. Diverging — its own item. Empty → inside the panel, a left-aligned empty state: a 40dp 2px-stroke line drawing in `edge-control`, a title.m headline ("Nothing to rank here"), one body line naming why, one ghost button. Never a centred shrug, never a card that renders at zero height. One item → a single row at full track width with no focus treatment at all: a ranking of one has no worst, and lighting the only bar would spend the product's one content amber on nothing. Two items → normal, focus on item 0. All values equal → every bar full length, focus still on item 0, and a meta line "All five are level at 34%"; identical bars without that sentence read as a rendering bug. All values zero → every row a 2dp stub, values "0", meta line "Nothing recorded in this window"; NOT the empty state, because five outlets with zero is a finding. Loading → 5 skeleton rows at the real geometry; after 600ms one Oatmeal rule travels the list's top edge. Error → the header renders, the body becomes the error line and one retry. Mixed null → rows with null values are dropped and the footer states "3 outlets had no visits and are not ranked", so the drop is visible.
items.behaviour: Stagger as per the row. On refresh bars animate from their previous fractions and the list does NOT re-sort under the reader's eyes — a new order arrives with a 200ms cross-fade of the whole list, so a row never appears to climb the ranking while being read. `MotionBudget.still`: instant, and the cross-fade becomes a cut.
items.modes: Night / Day / Veld per the row. Veld caps at 5 rows, not 8, and prints every value.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(container: true, label: 'Ranking: out-of-shelf availability by outlet, worst first, 8 of 20 shown')`. Each row announces its rank. "See the numbers" is the real accessibility path for the whole visual and is never hidden behind a menu. At 2.0× rows stack internally and the list grows; the cap stays at 8 because the cap is about argument, not space.
items.amber: At most one, and only the focus row's emitter, on the answered answer route. The list itself emits nothing: no amber title, no amber rule, no amber count, no amber overflow chevron.
items.screenshot: Under a small title and a grey "vs week 37", five rows of name-track-number on a dark panel, their bars stepping shorter down the list. On the answer screen the top bar is amber and faintly lit; everywhere else it is bone white and the rest are warm grey. At the bottom, a quiet grey line reading 12 more outlets, and beneath a hairline, a text button, See the numbers.

items.name: RankedBarList · diverging
items.purpose: The shape the list takes the moment any value is negative: movement around a zero, not magnitude from a baseline.
items.anatomy:
Triggered by `items.any((i) => i.value < 0)` — data-derived, never a caller's flag.

Centre axis: 1dp vertical rule at the track's midpoint, 16dp tall (the full 44dp row height is too loud). Colour: `flame-600` #FFB162 in Night IF the ledger grants it — this is a single 1dp rule shared by every row, one object rather than a repeated fill, and it is the one place the direction's "amber as a centre axis" survives. In Day and Veld the axis is ink-1 / veld-ink at 2px, because amber cannot be a line on a light ground (1.79:1 on white).

Positive bars grow right from the axis in `good`; negative bars grow LEFT in `bad` AND HATCHED — 45° RISING stripes, 3dp stripe on a 6dp period. The hatch exists because #FF7D8C against the neutral is 1.55:1 in true colour and 1.26:1 in protanopia; the stripe is the channel and the hue is the reinforcement.

**THE HATCH IS PAINTER LINES, NOT A GRADIENT DECORATION.** The first draft put a `TileMode.repeated` `LinearGradient` on every negative bar, and in a worst-first ranking most bars are negative — six of eight visible rows each constructing a fresh `BoxDecoration` and allocating a shader as they scroll in, inside the one list whose performance rule the same document had just written. The stripes are drawn as lines in the row's existing `CustomPainter`, which the registry already permits, so a diverging row costs zero extra decorations and the 12-gradients-per-screen budget has a test whose worst case is this exact list.

Every value is printed WITH its sign — `formatSignedAmount`, a true minus, an explicit plus on a rise — so direction never rides on which side of the axis a bar happens to be.

The focus row is still item 0. When it is negative, an amber fill would collide with the hatch, so the focus row's fill stays hatched `bad` and its channels become the origin marker, the weight, the bloom, and a 1.5dp `flame-600` outline around the bar's silhouette — bloom plus outline counted as one emitter.
items.states: Mixed signs. All negative → the axis sits hard right and every bar runs left; the axis is still drawn, because an axis at the edge is what tells you every value is below zero. All positive but diverging declared → impossible; the shape is data-derived. A zero in a diverging set → no bar, a 2dp mark ON the axis, and the value "0" printed — the existing code renders nothing for zero and this closes that hole. A value at exactly ±maxAbs → fills its half completely. Loading, empty, error, too-many → as the non-diverging list.
items.behaviour: Bars grow OUT FROM THE AXIS, both directions, 320ms, 40ms stagger — never from the left edge, which would animate a negative bar through positive territory. Stripes are fixed in world space while the bar's length animates, so they never appear to travel. `MotionBudget.still`: instant.
items.modes: Night: axis 1dp #FFB162 (granted) or ink-1, positive #6FE0AE at 7.04:1 on the track, negative hatched #FF7D8C at 4.65:1. Day: axis 2px #1B2632, positive #14664A at 5.03:1 on the Day track, negative hatched #8C1B2C at 6.60:1. Veld: axis 2px #1B2632, positive solid #0F5039, negative hatched #7A0F22 with 3dp stripes on a 10dp period on white, row 64dp, every value printed at 18/600.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(value: 'minus 19 percentage points')` — spoken as "minus", never as the glyph. The legend is mandatory in diverging mode and names both directions in words ("Fell", "Rose") with their swatch AND their fill pattern. At 2.0× rows stack, and in stacked form the axis becomes a 2dp horizontal rule above the track rather than a vertical one inside it. Non-colour: side of axis, hatch versus solid, printed sign, legend words.
items.amber: One at most, and it is the axis, not the focus row. With the answered route holding a single content slot the choice is forced and it is the right one: a diverging chart without a visible zero is unreadable, and the axis is shared by every row. The focus row then falls back to ink-1 outline plus marker plus weight.
items.screenshot: Five rows whose bars start from a thin amber line running down the middle of the panel. Two run right in mint; three run left in a soft red cut by tight diagonal stripes rising to the right, so even in a black-and-white print the left-hand bars are visibly a different material. Every number carries a plus or a true minus.

items.name: TrendChart
items.purpose: A current series, a dashed comparison, a target rule and a scrub — the one chart in the product that shows time.
items.anatomy:
Height 208dp (Field 232, Veld 180 with fewer points). Plot padding L 38, T 12, R 46, B 24, with the left gutter dynamic per ChartFrame.

CURRENT SERIES: 2dp stroke, round join and cap. `flame-600` #FFB162 in Night ONLY when the ledger grants it, which under the revised budget happens only on an answer that has no ranked bars to light; otherwise ink-1 #EEE9DF at 15.77:1 on the ground, which is how the Day chart already renders and reads perfectly well. Day: ink-1 #1B2632. Veld: veld-ink #0E141A at 3dp. Area fill beneath: a `LinearGradient` 12%→0 of the series colour in Night (capped down from the existing 28%, because a heavier wash behind the dashed terracotta comparison is the worst case for the tightest hue pair in the system), 8%→0 in Day, NONE in Veld.

COMPARISON SERIES: 1.5dp, dashed 4-3, `comparison` #E08E71 at 6.04:1 on the surface in Night, #A35139 at 5.18:1 in Day, #1B2632 dashed 8-6 at 2px in Veld. No fill, no endpoint label, no marker. The dashed/solid distinction is MANDATORY: simulated deuteranopia puts #FFB162 and #E08E71 1.41:1 apart, so the stroke pattern is doing all the work.

TARGET RULE: 1dp dashed 4-3 in `edge-control` (#7C93AC at 4.84:1 on the surface; #6E6657 Day; 2px #1B2632 Veld), labelled "Target 80" at meta 12 ink-3 in the right-hand gutter; if it would collide with the plot edge it moves above the rule at the left origin. NEVER amber — a target is a reference, not a light.

GRIDLINES: horizontal only, 1dp, `lifted` #2C3B4D Night, `hairline-decorative` #DED7C9 Day, NONE in Veld. Four ticks from `_niceScale`. Baseline 1dp `edge-control`.

ENDPOINT: a 4dp filled dot in the series colour with a 2dp ring in the panel's own surface, plus one direct label at figure.s 16/500 above-left. Every other value lives on the axis, in the scrub or in the table twin.

LEGEND: mandatory whenever there is more than one series.
items.states: One series. Two series. Fewer than 2 points → an honest empty plot at the same height, left-aligned: "Not enough to plot a trend" at body ink-2 plus one meta line naming the window, plus See the numbers. Exactly 2 points → drawn, both points labelled, and a meta line "Two buckets only" — a two-point line is a claim about a direction and the reader is entitled to know it rests on two readings. All values equal → a flat line at its true height labelled at both ends, never auto-scaled to invent variation. Gaps → a bucket with no visits produces NO point; the line breaks and the gap draws as a 3-3 dashed segment at 50% length coverage, with the missing bucket's axis label still printed. A gap is never interpolated. Comparison requested but empty → the subtitle says "no data for the month before" and no second line, no legend entry for a line that is not there. Low-sample bucket → a 4dp hollow circle with the segments either side dashed 3-3. Loading → the plot frame renders IMMEDIATELY at full value with a well-fill block where the series will be; the frame of reference is never the thing that is loading. Error → frame plus one line plus retry. Offline → cached, held chip in the cluster footer, and the last bucket carries "up to 14:02". Target absent → no rule, no ghost rule at 100 or at the mean.
items.behaviour:
The series draws left to right over 600ms ease-out-quart, clipped, with the chrome at full immediately. The endpoint dot and its label appear only at progress ≥ 0.995, so a label never floats ahead of its own data. Comparison draws inside the same clip, underneath. A new range re-draws rather than morphing. `MotionBudget.still`: instant.

THE SCRUB IS A HORIZONTAL-INTENT GESTURE, AND THE SPEC PICKS ONE SO THE IMPLEMENTER CANNOT PICK THE OTHER. The plot is 208dp of a vertically scrolling page; a recogniser that claims on the down-event kills scrolling over a third of the fold, and a manager who puts a thumb on the chart to scroll past it instead gets a readout that follows the thumb. So: a `HorizontalDragGestureRecognizer` enters the arena and the ancestor scrollable keeps vertical drags; the readout appears on the FIRST HORIZONTAL MOVEMENT, not on press, and the first draft's "appears instantly on press" is withdrawn as incompatible with a scrolling page. A plain tap that never becomes a drag opens the table twin — so the chart has a one-touch path to every value, which is better than the scrub it replaces. A `TrendChart` is never placed inside a horizontally scrolling ancestor; a test asserts it. Veld has no scrub at all: a tap anywhere opens the table twin, because a drag-readout in the sun with gloves is a fiction.
items.modes: Night: series amber only if granted and otherwise ink-1, 12% wash of whichever, terracotta dashed comparison, #2C3B4D gridlines, near-black ground. Day: ink-1 series, 8% wash, #A35139 dashed comparison, #DED7C9 gridlines, paper. Veld: 3px black series, no wash, 2px black dashed comparison at 8-6, no gridlines, max 5 plotted points with EVERY point labelled at figure.s 18/600, baseline 2px, height 180dp.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(container: true, label: 'On-shelf availability by week, eight weeks', value: 'From 74 percent to 61 percent, a fall of 13 points; target 80')` — the trend is described in words as the first-class path and the scrub is an enhancement. Every value is reachable from the axis or the table twin, so nothing is gated behind a gesture. The plot is a ≥44dp-tall touch region across its full width. At 2.0× the axis gutter grows, tick labels thin to 2 rather than overlap, and the legend stacks one per line. Non-colour: stroke pattern, endpoint marker, legend words, direct labels.
items.amber: At most one in Night — the current series stroke together with its area wash, one emitter — and only when the answer route's single content slot is not already spent on a ranked-bar focus. On the dashboard, on every agent screen, in Day and in Veld the series is ink-1. The comparison, target, gridlines, axis and endpoint ring are never amber.
items.screenshot: On a dark panel, a line rising then falling across eight weeks — amber with a soft haze beneath it on an answer with no ranking, bone white on the dashboard — a dashed terracotta line tracking lower behind it, a faint dashed grey rule labelled Target 80 crossing near the top, four horizontal hairlines, and the last point marked with a small dot and 61% in monospace above it.

items.name: ScrubReadout
items.purpose: What the finger reads while it drags: the value under the caret, its movement, and the comparison bucket it is actually aligned to.
items.anatomy:
A `raised` block (Night #22303E, Day #F4F0E8), radius 10, padding 10dp × 8dp, width 176dp, with a 1px `edge-control` outline — #7C93AC at 4.25:1 on `raised`, NOT `edge-structure`, which measures 2.63:1 there and would have been a sub-3:1 edge on a floating object. No shadow in Night, sh2 in Day.

Top to bottom: bucket label at eyebrow 11/700 ink-2, uppercase — s1 4dp — a baseline row of [FigureSlot figure.m 22 mono ink-1 at 11.12:1] s2 8dp [Delta against the previous point] — s1 4dp — series name at meta 12 ink-3 at 5.07:1 — s1 4dp — the comparison line: its VALUE and its OWN BUCKET LABEL in mono meta, because the two series are aligned by position and not by date and the reader is entitled to see which bucket they are being shown.

Crosshair: a 1dp vertical rule in `edge-control` from plot top to baseline, plus a 4.5dp dot with a 2dp surface-coloured ring on the current series.

POSITION: 12dp right of the caret, clamped inside the plot, flipping left past the plot midpoint so the readout never covers the point it describes.
items.states: Active. First point (no previous) → the delta slot is absent, not zero. Gap bucket → "No visits in week 34", crosshair still drawn; a gap is scrubbable and that is the point. No comparison → the line is absent and the readout shrinks; it does not render an em dash for a series that was never requested. Low-sample bucket → "from 2 visits" in meta and the delta suppressed. Docked → when the readout's width exceeds 60% of the plot width, which 2.0× reliably causes, it stops floating and docks as a full-width block immediately BELOW the plot, crosshair still following the finger. Released → dismissed on drag end and tap up. Veld → does not exist.
items.behaviour: Appears on the first horizontal movement, with no fade — a readout that animates in lags the finger, and the entry threshold is the gesture's, not a delay of its own. Follows the caret with no easing. Dismisses on release. Haptic: a 10ms selection tick at each index change, suppressed when `MotionBudget.still`. The nearest-index snap is across the full plot width, so the finger never has to find a dot.
items.modes: Night `raised` #22303E with ink-1 at 11.12:1 and ink-3 at 5.07:1 — the binding case for 12px meta in the whole system, and it passes. Day `raised` #F4F0E8 with ink-3 at 5.48:1, sh2. Veld: none.
items.accessibility: Not a screen-reader path at all — it is a pointer and touch enhancement, so the whole readout is `ExcludeSemantics`, and the chart's own semantics plus the table twin carry every value it can show. An announcing tooltip that follows a drag produces a stream of interruptions. At 2.0× it docks. Its contents are never the only place a value exists.
items.amber: None. Crosshair, dot ring and delta are neutral or severity-coded. An amber crosshair would be a second emitter measuring the first one.
items.screenshot: A small dark slab floating over the chart, WEEK 36 in tiny oatmeal caps at the top, 68% beneath it in monospace with a small red triangle and −3 beside it, then in grey, On-shelf availability, then 71% · Aug 2024 (same month last year).

items.name: ChartLegend
items.purpose: The rule, not the caveat: every multi-series chart renders a legend showing swatch AND stroke pattern, every time.
items.anatomy:
A `Wrap`, spacing s3 12dp, runSpacing s1 4dp, left-aligned to the plot's left gutter, ABOVE the plot with s2 8dp beneath it.

Each item: a 14×3dp swatch — solid for a solid series, or two 5dp segments with a 4dp gap for a dashed one, at the SAME dash ratio the series uses — then s2 8dp, then the label at label 13/500 ink-2 (8.57:1 on the Night surface, 9.04:1 on the Day card), `Flexible` with a single-line ellipsis. The label is a sentence the server writes — "the month to date before this one" — and an inflexible `Text` overflows a `Wrap`.

For a bar chart with a fill distinction the swatch is a 14×8dp rectangle carrying the actual fill: solid, hatched or outlined, at the same stripe period.

Ellipsis rather than a second line, because the legend sits directly above the plot and growing it downward shifts the chart under the reader's eyes at exactly the widths where there is least room.
items.states: Two series. Three or more → monochrome `chart-neutral` at stepped alpha PLUS distinct stroke patterns (solid, 4-3, 1-3, 6-2), never a generated hue ramp; the pattern is the primary channel and the alpha is reinforcement. One series → no legend; a legend naming one thing is chrome. Series present but empty → no entry; the legend never names a line that is not on the chart. Focus-bar legend → one entry, "The outlet this answer is about", with the focus channel's actual swatch — amber where the ledger granted it, ink-1 everywhere else, so the legend can never claim a colour the chart did not draw. Diverging → two entries, "Rose" solid and "Fell" hatched, in words. Truncated label → ellipsis, and the full label is in the table twin's header. Loading → labels render as soon as the series NAMES are known, swatches at well fill.
items.behaviour: No motion. Not interactive by default; on a chart with more than two series, tapping a legend item drops the others to 40% alpha AND to a 1dp stroke — two channels — and the toggle state is announced. Never hides a series entirely; hiding is how a chart lies.
items.modes: Night: swatches in the actual series colours, labels ink-2. Day: same structure, no amber swatch, because there is no amber series on paper. Veld: swatch 20×4dp, label 16/600 veld-ink-2, items always stacked one per line, never wrapped inline.
items.accessibility: Each item is a `Semantics` node reading "solid amber line: this period" / "dashed terracotta line: the month before" — the pattern is in the string, so a screen-reader user gets the same distinction a dichromat gets. At 2.0× items stack one per line and the ellipsis gives way to wrapping, because at that size the chart has already grown and the shift is acceptable. Not a tap target unless interactive, in which case 44/48/56dp.
items.amber: Inherited, never new: if the current series is amber, its swatch is the same amber and is part of that same emitter. A legend never introduces amber of its own, and when the series falls back to ink-1 the swatch falls back with it.
items.screenshot: Above the plot, two small marks side by side: a short solid dash followed by This period, then a gap, then two tiny terracotta dashes followed by The month before this one — both labels in warm grey at reading size.

items.name: ChartFrame
items.purpose: The shared geometry every plot is drawn into — padding, scale, ticks, baseline, target rule — so two charts on one screen have the same left edge and the same tick logic.
items.anatomy:
Padding: line and area plots L38 T12 R46 B24; column plots L38 T12 R10 B24; horizontal bar plots L92 T6 R46 B22 — existing values, already consistent and already tested.

Left gutter is DYNAMIC: `max(declared, widestTickLabelWidth + 8dp)`, measured with a `TextPainter` at the current `TextScaler` — and measured by calling `TextScaler.scale(size)` per size, never by multiplying a factor, since Android 14's non-linear scaling makes a factor wrong at both ends. This is the single most common 2.0× failure in charts and it is fixed at the frame, once.

Scale: `_niceScale` unchanged — round the range out to nice bounds, 4 ticks, 18% padding so the line never rides an edge, `forceMin` to pull the target inside the plot. A range whose hi−lo is below 1e-9 is given hi = lo + 1 rather than dividing by zero.

Ticks: 4 by default, dropping to 2 when label height × 4 exceeds 60% of the plot height, never overlapping. Tick labels at meta 12 ink-3 mono, right-aligned 8dp off the plot's left edge.

X labels: first, middle, last only, left/centre/right aligned so the first and last never overhang.

Baseline: 1dp `edge-control`. Gridlines: horizontal only, 1dp `lifted` Night, `hairline-decorative` Day, none in Veld.

Target rule: 1dp dashed 4-3 `edge-control`, labelled in the right gutter. A target is the one legitimately dashed rule in the system — it IS a threshold. Nothing else dashes except a comparison series.

ZERO BASELINE RULE: any chart whose marks are FILLED (bars, columns, areas) must include zero in its scale. Only stroked line charts may use a non-zero baseline, and when they do, the lowest tick label is the proof. Asserted by a test.
items.states: Normal. 2.0× → gutter grows, ticks thin. Very wide (Console ≥1080) → gutter 40dp, plot padding unchanged, the plot simply widens; marks never stretch past a 2.5dp stroke cap. Very narrow (<300dp) → tick labels drop to 2, x labels to first and last. All-zero data → scale 0…1 with a single tick at 0 and a meta line naming the absence. Negative range → the scale spans it and the zero line draws as a 1dp `edge-control` rule, heavier than a gridline. Veld → no gridlines, 2px baseline, ticks only at min and max.
items.behaviour: Chrome paints immediately at full value on every render; only the data animates. The frame of reference is never the thing that is animating — the rule that makes a re-drawing chart legible rather than disorienting. Repaint is gated on data, scale, caret and skin only.
items.modes: Night gridlines #2C3B4D, baseline #7C93AC at 4.84:1 on the surface. Day gridlines #DED7C9, baseline #6E6657 at 5.31:1. Veld: no gridline, baseline 2px #1B2632, tick labels 14/600 veld-ink-2.
items.accessibility: The frame is `ExcludeSemantics`; the chart's container semantics describe the range and the target in words ("scale from 40 to 100 percent, target 80"), because gridlines are not readable objects. At 2.0× everything above. Non-colour: the frame carries no meaning by hue at all.
items.amber: None, ever — no amber gridline, axis, target rule or tick. The frame is where a designer is most tempted to brand a chart, and where the brand must be absent so the one emitter inside it reads as light.
items.screenshot: An empty plot: four faint horizontal rules, four small grey numbers down the left, a slightly brighter rule along the bottom with three date labels beneath it, and one dashed grey rule crossing near the top with Target 80 in the right margin.

items.name: Sparkline
items.purpose: A trend cue at row scale — 64dp of shape at the right end of a worklist row, where the row's figure is the reading and the line is only the direction.
items.anatomy:
64×20dp (Field 72×24, Veld 80×28). No axes, no labels, no fill, no target.

Stroke 1.5dp (Veld 2.5dp), round join and cap, `chart-neutral` #A39887 Night, #5C5648 Day, #4A4437 Veld. Never the series colour, and never amber: five rows each with an amber dot was a named error in the direction — it put eight amber objects on a screen that claimed three.

LAST POINT: a 3dp filled dot in THAT ROW'S SEVERITY colour — `good` #6FE0AE, `bad` #FF7D8C, or ink-3 for neutral. Colour that already encodes something costs nothing; a new hue would cost a channel.

Normalised to its own min/max with a 2dp inset top and bottom so the extremes are not clipped.

Each sparkline lives in a `RepaintBoundary` and caches to a `Picture` invalidated only on data change — 40 of them in a scrolling list must cost one paint each, not one per frame.
items.states: Normal. Flat (all values equal) → a solid horizontal line at mid-height with its dot; a true reading, and it must look different from an absence. Fewer than 2 points → the box keeps its exact footprint so the row does not jump the day the series shrinks, and renders a centred em dash at meta ink-3 — NOT a dashed flat line, which reads as "flat". Single spike → drawn as-is; no smoothing, no clamping. Gap → the segment dashes 2-2 rather than interpolating. Low sample → the whole line dashes 3-3 and the dot is hollow. Loading → a well-fill block at the exact footprint. Error → the em dash, same as too-few-points; a row does not stop rendering because its sparkline failed. Pressed → inherits the row.
items.behaviour: No entry animation at all inside a list — 40 animating sparklines on a 2 GB Android is the frame budget gone. In the one place a sparkline appears outside a list (an outlet header) it draws left to right over 320ms. No hover, no scrub, no tooltip: the row's figure and the row's tap carry it.
items.modes: Night stroke #A39887 at 5.40:1 on the surface, dot in severity. Day stroke #5C5648 at 6.82:1. Veld stroke 2.5dp #4A4437, dot 4dp in #0F5039 / #7A0F22, box 80×28 — and in Veld the sparkline is the FIRST thing dropped when the row runs out of width, because a 2mm line in the sun is decoration.
items.accessibility: `ExcludeSemantics` on the drawing; the owning row's semantics carry the direction in words — "down 19 points over five weeks" — which is the only form of a sparkline a screen reader can use. Never the sole carrier of anything: the row always prints the figure and the severity word. At 2.0× the box does not scale but the row grows around it, and below 300dp of row width it is dropped entirely rather than squeezed.
items.amber: None. This is the most-repeated data mark in the product and therefore the one place a repeated amber fill would most decisively break the law.
items.screenshot: At the right end of a worklist row, a small warm-grey line falling gently across about two centimetres, ending in a tiny soft-red dot; to its left, the row's figure in monospace.

items.name: ScoreMark — and the death of the gauge
items.purpose: The compact form of a score where a full hero will not fit — an outlet card, a list row, an agent scorecard. It is a meter, a figure and a band word, because the arc it replaces was a gauge invented for completeness.
items.anatomy:
**The 96dp ScoreArc is cut, now, before anyone writes the `CustomPainter`.** It had no call site in the codebase, it cost a `drawArc` per instance, it capped at 8 per list and silently became a Meter beyond that — so the same outlet showed a ring in a list of six and a bar in a list of nine, and a manager scrolling territories watched the score change shape for reasons that had nothing to do with the score. Everything it carried, the meter and the band word already carry. Taking the decision here costs one paragraph; taking it at goldens costs a component.

ScoreMark is a row, not a square. Height 64dp (Field 72, Veld 88).

Line 1, a baseline `Row`: [FigureSlot figure.l 32 mono ink-1] s1 4dp ["/100" Onest 14/600 ink-3] s3 12dp [severity glyph 7dp] s2 8dp [band WORD at label 13/500 in the band's ink] — and where the row has an owner, [name, body 15/400, `Expanded`, before all of it].
Line 2, at s2 8dp: a Meter at 6dp with the 80-point standard as a 2dp ink-1 tick breaking the track's top edge.

COMMITMENT BY SHAPE, NOT BY HUE ALONE — the severity grammar applied to a bar: Healthy → solid `good` fill plus a 7dp filled circle. Watch → `bad` fill drawn as a 1.5dp OUTLINE plus a 7dp half-filled triangle. Gap → solid `bad-solid` fill plus a 7dp filled triangle plus a 3dp bar on the owning row's left edge. Note that `bad-solid` #E23C55 measures 2.72:1 against the Night track and is therefore a BLOCK colour, never a thin mark on a track — at Gap the fill is full-height and full-commitment, which is exactly when a block is right.
