Solid / outline / solid-other-hue with three distinct glyphs survives greyscale, both common dichromacies and a sun-washed panel.
items.states: Healthy / Watch / Gap as above. Not scored → the track carries the not-measured hatch full width, an em dash in the figure slot, and the words "Not scored" — no fill at zero length, which would read as a score of 0. Zero score → a genuine 0 draws a 2dp stub, reads "0", and takes the Gap treatment. Over 100 → the fill completes with a 2dp ink-1 cap; the figure is authoritative. Provisional → the fill draws as a 1.5dp outline of its own colour plus the dotted underline on the figure. Loading → outlined track, well-fill figure block, no glyph, no word. Error → outlined track, em dash, "Couldn't load". Pressed → the full row is the target, 120ms `lifted` fill.
items.behaviour: The bar grows from the origin over 320ms in step with the figure's count-up so the number and the length agree at every frame. `MotionBudget.still`: instant. Tap opens the dimension breakdown. Costs one `DecoratedBox` and two `Text`s per row, so a list of thirty is a list of thirty rows rather than thirty arcs, and no substitution rule is needed at any length.
items.modes: Night: track `lifted` #2C3B4D, `good` #6FE0AE at 7.04:1 on it, `bad` outline #FF7D8C at 4.65:1, `bad-solid` #E23C55 as a block only, figure ink-1. Day: track #E2DBCC, #14664A at 5.03:1, #8C1B2C at 6.60:1, #7A0F22, figure #1B2632. Veld: track white with a 2px border, fills #0F5039 (9.43:1) and #7A0F22 (10.94:1) at 8dp, Watch drawn as a 2px outline, figure 34/600, band word 16/600, row 88dp.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(label: 'Perfect-store score', value: '71 out of 100, Watch', hint: 'Target 80. Double tap for the six dimensions')`. The band word is in the value, so hue and fill pattern are reinforcements. Tap target 64/72/88dp. At 2.0× the figure re-picks its role by measurement, the band word wraps beneath, and the row grows.
items.amber: None. A score is the most severity-laden number in the product and severity abandons amber's hue band entirely. The wire's band value 'amber' maps to the word "Watch" and the outlined-crimson commitment level — see Open questions.
items.screenshot: A list row on dark ground: an outlet name at the left, then 71 in large monospace with a small grey /100 at its shoulder, then a half-filled red triangle and the word Watch. Beneath, a short track two-thirds filled with a thin hollow red outline rather than a solid, and a pale tick standing proud of it at the 80 mark.

items.name: ScoreHero
items.purpose: The moment the visit is worth landing: the weighted total, the band in words, and the movement since this agent's last visit to this store.
items.anatomy:
Left-aligned to the gutter, NOT centred — the existing screen centres this and it is the one composition change the direction insists on. No card in Night (the ground carries it); a Panel in Day; a white block with a 2px #1B2632 border in Veld.

Top to bottom: eyebrow "PERFECT-STORE SCORE" 11/700/+8% ink-2 — s2 8dp — a `Wrap` (crossAxisAlignment end, spacing s3 12dp, runSpacing s2 8dp) holding [FigureSlot hero.figure 72 mono ink-1 at 15.77:1] + ["/100" Onest 20/600 ink-3] and, as a second Wrap child so it drops to its own line under pressure, [the band cluster] — s5 20dp — BandScale — s4 16dp — the movement line.

BAND CLUSTER: a 7dp severity glyph (filled circle / half-filled triangle / filled triangle), s2 8dp, the band WORD at title.m 16/600 in the band's ink. Word first, colour second, always.

MOVEMENT LINE: a Delta in neutral-or-sentiment, then the sentence in body ink-2: "Up 6 points from your last visit here (65)." Unchanged reads "Same as your last visit here (71)." at body ink-3 with the flat bar glyph — never "+0".

The hero figure is the ONE role in the system with a `TextScaler` exception: it caps at an effective 1.6×, documented in the token rather than hidden in a wrapper, because above that no fitting rule saves a 72dp number on a 360dp screen. The cap is applied by clamping the SCALED SIZE returned by `TextScaler.scale(72)`, not by multiplying 72 by a factor, so it behaves correctly under Android's non-linear curve. Everything else on this screen scales to 2.0×.
items.states: Scored. Held on this phone → the whole hero is replaced by the existing receipt: a tick mark, "Sent from your phone", the held banner, and the sentence explaining that the real score appears when it reaches the server. No number is invented — `visit_outcome_screen.dart` and the string `outcomeNoGuess` exist because someone decided an agent shown 74 in the shop who finds 68 in the morning will not trust the third number, and that decision is kept here until it is overturned deliberately. Scoring in progress → eyebrow and BandScale render; the figure is a well-fill block at the width of "100"; three 6dp Oatmeal dots travel on a 600ms loop beneath it; never a spinner. Unreachable → the same receipt with the unreachable wording. No previous visit → the movement line is absent entirely, not "—". Band missing → glyph and word omitted, BandScale still renders with its marker; a score without a band is still a score.
items.behaviour: The figure counts up 600ms ease-out-quart from zero — the one count-from-zero in the product, correct here because the score genuinely did not exist a second ago — inside a slot width-reserved at three glyphs for the duration, so the "/100", the glyph and the band word do not sit 43dp to the left and then slide right during the most important moment in the agent's day. The BandScale marker travels over the same 600ms and arrives together. `MotionBudget.still`: instant. The band word never animates. Tapping the hero scrolls to the dimension breakdown and flashes its first row's `lifted` fill for 200ms. Back from this screen means "on to the next store".
items.modes: Night: ground #0B1017, figure at 15.77:1, `good` #6FE0AE 11.76:1, `bad` #FF7D8C 7.78:1. Day: Palladian, figure #1B2632 12.67:1, `good` #14664A 5.73:1, `bad` #8C1B2C 7.52:1. Veld: white, hero figure stays 72 — the one hero Veld keeps, because outdoors a score is exactly the thing that must be readable at arm's length — band word 18/600, glyph 10dp, BandScale 12dp tall with 2px divisions, movement line 17/600, and every severity ink clears 9:1 (#0F5039 at 9.43, #7A0F22 at 10.94).
items.accessibility: `Semantics(label: 'Perfect-store score', value: '71 out of 100, Watch, up 6 points from your last visit here which was 65')` — one utterance, the whole outcome. The figure and the band word are a single semantics node so they cannot be read apart. At 1.6× the figure holds; the band cluster drops to its own line via the Wrap; the BandScale labels wrap. At 2.0× everything but the figure scales. Non-colour: the band word, the glyph silhouette, the marker's position on the scale, the movement sentence.
items.amber: None. Not the figure, not the band, not the scale, not the delta. This screen has exactly one amber object and it is the primary action at the bottom — "Next store" — and only in Day and Veld, where amber is a block you press.
items.screenshot: On near-black, small oatmeal caps PERFECT-STORE SCORE, and beneath it hung off the left gutter an enormous off-white 71 in monospace with a small /100 at its shoulder, then to the right at the same baseline a half-filled red triangle and the word Watch. Below, a flat rule split into three by two upright threshold marks, with a bright pale marker standing on it, and under that: a small green triangle, Up 6 points, and in grey, from your last visit here (65).

items.name: BandScale
items.purpose: Where this score sits on the published banding — the thing that turns a bare 71 into 'nine points below healthy'.
items.anatomy:
**The three alpha washes are deleted.** They measured, over the Night track, 1.72:1 for Gap, 1.30:1 for Watch and 2.18:1 for Healthy, with Gap and Watch — two adjacent severity bands — only 1.32:1 apart from each other and the same hue. That is one hue at two alpha steps carrying the whole distinction, which is the exact mechanism this surface deletes `DeltaChip` for three items earlier, and in daylight through a scratched protector the Watch segment simply vanished, leaving a two-block rule whose marker appeared to stand in the gap.

What replaces them is nothing, which is the right answer. The scale is:

A horizontal rule, height 8dp (Field 10, Veld 12), radius 4 (Veld 0), full content width, in the track colour, with a 1px `edge-structure` outline so it is visible when nothing is inside it.

THRESHOLD MARKS at each published boundary: 2dp wide, ink-1, running the full height and BREAKING BOTH EDGES by 3dp — the same silhouette mechanism as the meter's target tick, and the reason it works here is the reason it works there: a threshold is a mark, not a region. Two marks, three bands, no fills.

MARKER: 3dp wide, 16dp tall, radius 2, ink-1, standing proud by 4dp above and below, clamped so it never leaves the track. NO glow, no `BoxShadow` — the existing white 10dp-blur shadow is deleted, since Night has no coloured shadows anywhere.

LABELS beneath at s2 8dp, meta 12 ink-3 (Veld 14/600), one per band, left/centre/right aligned to their spans: "GAP <70", "70–79", "HEALTHY 80+". Thresholds come from the client's published banding, never hardcoded.

The severity HUE appears exactly once on this screen and it is the band word in the hero cluster above. The scale's job is position; the word's job is verdict; neither does the other's.

Deliberately NOT used here: the registry's hatch, dot and outline patterns. Those four fills are spoken for — not-measured, negative, low-sample, provisional — and spending one on "the Gap band" would give a single material two meanings on a single screen. The registry's cap is only a cap if it is honoured by its own author's next idea.
items.states: Normal. Score at a boundary → the marker sits exactly on the threshold mark and the band word resolves by the published rule (≥, not >), stated in the provenance sheet. Score 0 → marker at the far left, fully visible, not clipped. Score 100 → marker at the far right, fully visible. Score > 100 → marker clamped to the right end with a 3-notch cut drawn beyond it. No score → the rule renders with its outline, its threshold marks and its labels, and NO marker; there is nothing to place, and the labels alone still tell an agent what the bands are. Banding not published → the scale is omitted entirely rather than invented; the band word alone carries it. Loading → rule, marks and labels render (thresholds are known before the score), marker absent. 2.0× → labels wrap to two lines each and the label row grows; the rule does not scale.
items.behaviour: The marker travels from the left origin to its position over 600ms in step with the hero's count-up; it never jumps. `MotionBudget.still`: placed instantly. Not interactive; tapping the hero opens the provenance sheet, which explains the banding in words.
items.modes: Night: track `lifted` #2C3B4D with a 1px #5A7088 outline, marks and marker #EEE9DF at 9.43:1 on the track. Day: track #E2DBCC with a 1px #6E6657 outline (4.12:1 — `edge-structure` is not used on the Day well), marks and marker #1B2632 at 11.12:1. Veld: track white with a 2px #1B2632 border, threshold marks 3px #0E141A breaking both edges by 4dp, marker 4px × 20dp solid, labels 14/600.
items.accessibility: `ExcludeSemantics` on the drawing; the hero's value string already carries "71 out of 100, Watch", and the provenance sheet carries the banding in sentences. Never the only place the band is stated. At 2.0× as above.
items.amber: None. A banded scale is a severity object end to end.
items.screenshot: A short flat rule under the big score, faintly outlined, crossed by two upright pale marks that stand slightly above and below it, and one taller brighter marker standing just left of the second mark. Three small grey labels beneath: GAP <70, 70–79, HEALTHY 80+.

items.name: DimensionBreakdown
items.purpose: How the score was made: six named dimensions, each with its figure, its bar against the 80-point standard, and an honest hatch where nothing could be measured.
items.anatomy:
A Panel of 6 rows (the keys are the API's: availability, visibility, display, pricing, competitive → "Share of shelf", salesCapability → "Team capability"), separated by 1px hairlines, last row undivided.

Row: padding s4 16dp × s3 12dp (Field 20/16, Veld 24/20), min height 64dp (Veld 88dp).

Line 1, a baseline `Row`: [dimension name, body 15/400 ink-1, `Expanded`, wrapping to 2 lines] s3 12dp [FigureSlot figure.s 16/500 mono] s2 8dp [weight at meta 12 ink-3 mono, "×0.25"].

Line 2, at s2 8dp: a 5dp bar (Field 6, Veld 8), radius 3, track `lifted` / `well` / white-with-2px-border with the empty-track outline rule, fill `chart-neutral` #A39887 at 4.02:1 in the measured case — NOT a severity hue per dimension, because six severity-coloured bars in one panel is six severity objects and the score's own band has already delivered the verdict. The 80-point standard is a 2dp ink-1 tick breaking the track's top edge by 2dp.

Line 3, only when there is something to say: the unmeasurable reason at meta 12 ink-3, wrapping freely.

WEIGHTS are printed because a weighted total nobody can decompose is a number you cannot act on, and the weights are the decomposition.
items.states: Measured. NOT MEASURED → its own item; em dash, full-width falling hatch, reason line. Zero → "0", a 2dp stub at the origin, and — the distinction the whole component exists for — NO reason line, because a zero was measured. Above 80 → the fill continues past the tick with a 2dp ink-1 cap. Weight zero (a dimension this client does not score) → the row is omitted and the footer states "This client does not score Display." Unknown dimension key → rendered with the repository's English fallback label rather than hidden. Loading → six rows at real geometry with well-fill blocks and outlined tracks, reason lines absent. Error → the panel renders one line and a retry; rows do not each fail. Offline → cached scorecard with the held chip in the footer. Reveal → rows arrive at a 40ms stagger on a 200ms enter, capped so the sixth starts at 200ms.
items.behaviour: Bars grow from the origin over 320ms with the row stagger, after the hero's count-up has finished — the breakdown explains a number that has already landed. `MotionBudget.still`: instant. Each row is tappable at ≥64dp and opens what that dimension counted ("12 SKUs checked, 2 out of stock"), which is the link between the score and the capture the agent actually did. Long-press copies the row.
items.modes: Night: panel `surface` #1B2632 with a #5A7088 edge at 3.00:1, rows divided by #3A4B60, figures ink-1 at 12.67:1, bars #A39887 on #2C3B4D. Day: #FAF7F2 panel, #DED7C9 dividers, #5C5648 bars on #E2DBCC. Veld: white, 2px #1B2632 dividers and border, 8dp bars in #4A4437 on white with a 2px border, tick 3px #0E141A breaking 3dp, name 17/600, figure 18/600, reason 14/600, row 88dp — and Veld shows only the dimensions that were measured plus a count of those that were not, because six rows at 88dp is three screens outdoors.
items.accessibility: Each row is a `Semantics` node: "Availability, 84 out of 100, weight 0.25, above the 80 standard". An unmeasured row announces "Availability, not measured, no competitor on shelf, not counted against you" — never "dash". The panel container announces "Six dimensions, four measured". At 2.0× names take two lines, figures re-pick their role, reasons wrap, rows grow. Non-colour: the hatch pattern, the tick silhouette, the em dash, the reason sentence, the weight.
items.amber: None. Six rows each with an amber standard-tick would be six amber objects on a route budgeted for none — and this panel is half the reason the Meter's tick is ink-1 everywhere.
items.screenshot: A dark outlined panel of six rows. Each row: a name at the left, a monospace number and a small grey ×0.25 at the right, and beneath them a thin track with a warm-grey fill and a pale tick standing proud at the 80 mark. The fifth row has a long dash where the number should be, a track filled edge to edge with fine falling diagonal lines, and a grey sentence under it, No competitor on shelf — not counted against you.

items.name: NotMeasured · the hatch
items.purpose: The fourth state the product has been missing: not zero, not missing, not an error — we could not confirm this, and it is not counted against you.
items.anatomy:
Applied to a BAR OR A TRACK. Never to a glyph, and the reason is below.

FILL: the track colour, then 45° FALLING stripes (top-left to bottom-right), 1.2dp wide at a 5dp period, in `edge-control`: Night #7C93AC at 3.60:1 on the #2C3B4D track, Day #6E6657 at 4.12:1 on #E2DBCC, Veld 2px #1B2632 at an 8dp period on white. Drawn as lines in the owning row's existing `CustomPainter`, or as a hard-stop repeating `LinearGradient` on a non-scrolling child — never a shader, never a blur, and inside a builder row always the painter form.

SPANS THE FULL TRACK, ALWAYS. This is the load-bearing rule: a partial hatched bar reads as a hatched VALUE. Full-width hatch plus an em dash above it says "there is no measurement here", and nothing else can. The track also takes its 1px `edge-structure` outline, since a hatched track has no fill to define it.

DIRECTION IS A DISTINCTION: not-measured hatch FALLS (↘); the diverging negative hatch RISES (↗) and is `bad`-coloured at a 6dp period. The two never appear in the same object but they appear on the same screen, and they must not be the same material.

PAIRED ALWAYS with an em dash in the figure slot and a reason line in words when the server knows one.
items.states: Not measured, reason known ("No competitor on shelf"). Not measured, reason unknown → "Not measured in this visit" — never blank, because a hatch with no sentence is a puzzle. **CAN'T CONFIRM (ticket #375) IS NOT A HATCH.** The first draft put this 1.2dp/5dp-period stripe inside the visit hub's ~20dp section glyph, which breaks the registry's own rule that a pattern on a mark under 4dp is aliasing — five stripes inside a 20dp disc at 40% brightness render as a flat mid-grey disc, which is visually the half-filled circle that already means "partly captured", and Veld's coarsened period gives the disc two stripes, which reads as a rendering artefact. So "can't confirm" is a FOURTH GLYPH in the section ladder, not a hatched third one: a ring at the empty ring's stroke weight with a 2dp diagonal bar through it, plus the words "Can't confirm" on the row, plus the explicit sentence that the section is excluded from the readiness count. Four glyphs — tick, half-circle, empty ring, barred ring — are four silhouettes, which is what the ladder needed. Not applicable (a dimension this client does not score) → NOT hatched; the row is omitted and named in the footer, because "we don't score this" and "we couldn't measure this" are different claims. Not yet measured (the visit is open) → NOT hatched; an empty ring, which is the ladder's own not-started state. Loading → not hatched; a well-fill block.
items.behaviour: Never animates — there is nothing to grow to, and a hatch growing from the left would read as a value arriving. Painted at full extent on the first frame. Does not respond to press separately from its row. On tap, the row's sheet leads with the reason and, where one exists, the action that would produce a measurement next time.
items.modes: Night #7C93AC on #2C3B4D. Day #6E6657 on #E2DBCC. Veld 2px #1B2632 on white at an 8dp period — coarser, because a 5dp period at arm's length in glare reads as a flat grey, which is the same reason it cannot live inside a 20dp glyph.
items.accessibility: The hatch carries NO semantics of its own; its owning row announces "not measured" plus the reason. That is the point: the visual encoding is for sighted users and the sentence is for everyone, and neither is a fallback for the other. At 2.0× the period does not change but the em dash and the reason scale and wrap. Non-colour: the stripe pattern is itself the non-colour channel, and it survives greyscale, both dichromacies, print and a sun-washed panel.
items.amber: None. An unmeasured dimension is the most tempting "warning" in the product and it is not a warning at all — it is an absence, and the system's absence colour is ink-3 and a pattern.
items.screenshot: Where the other rows have a solid warm-grey bar two-thirds across a dark track, this row's track is filled corner to corner with fine pale diagonals falling left to right, and above it, where a number would be, one long dash. On the visit hub, a section row carries neither a tick nor a half-circle but a ring with a single diagonal bar struck through it, and the words Can't confirm.

items.name: Provisional and final
items.purpose: Ticket #377: a figure the phone computed and a figure the server scored are different claims, and when they disagree the product must say so in one line instead of quietly changing the number.
items.anatomy:
PROVISIONAL MARKER, on any figure: a 2dp DOTTED underline (2dp on, 2dp off) in ink-3, 4dp below the mono run's baseline box, spanning the run's width only. Plus the word "Provisional" at meta 12 ink-3 with a 7dp hollow-circle glyph, placed where the delta would be. The figure stays ink-1 and full size — dimming a provisional number would imply it is less legible rather than less final.

No count-up on a provisional figure. Count-up is the gesture of arrival.

RECONCILIATION BLOCK, when a final figure replaces a provisional one that DIFFERS by more than the metric's rounding: a `well` block (Night #141D27, Day #E2DBCC, Veld white with a 2px border), radius 10 at the bottom corners and 0 at the top, a 1px `edge-control` outline (#7C93AC at 5.37:1 on the Night well; #6E6657 at 4.12:1 on the Day well, since `edge-structure` measures 2.99:1 there and is not used), padding s4 16dp, directly under the figure it reconciles.

Three lines:
1. "Final 71" — label 13/500 ink-2 (9.51:1 on the Night well) + FigureSlot figure.m 22 mono ink-1 (14.06:1).
2. "On your phone 84" — label 13/500 ink-3 (6.41:1 on the Night well, 4.52:1 on the Day well) + FigureSlot figure.m 22 mono ink-3, with a HOLLOW 8dp triangle (1.5dp stroke, ink-3) showing the direction between the two. **Never coloured good or bad**, and never struck through: this delta is a reconciliation, not a performance movement, and colouring it would tell an agent they got worse when what happened is that the arithmetic changed.
3. The reason, in body ink-2, from the server: "Two sections' photos arrived after scoring." / "Share of shelf could not be measured, so it is no longer in the total."

No strikethrough anywhere — a 1dp strike at 40% backlight vanishes, and a struck number reads as an error the agent made.
items.states: Provisional only (no final yet) → marker and word, no block. Final with no provisional ever shown → nothing at all. Final agrees within rounding → no block; a quiet meta line "Confirmed" with a filled circle, which is the reassurance an agent actually wants. Final differs → the block. Final differs and is LOWER → identical treatment; direction is in the hollow triangle and the reason, and the tone does not change. Final never arrives (still held) → the current product's behaviour is preserved: no number at all on the outcome screen, with the receipt and `outcomeNoGuess`. Provisional AND low sample → both markers; the dotted underline and the hollow square are different channels. Dismissed → a 44dp ghost "Got it"; the block does not return for that visit, and the marker on the figure persists in history.
items.behaviour: The block arrives with a 320ms enter when the final lands, pushing content below it down — never replacing the number in place, which is exactly the silent change this exists to prevent. The figure above does NOT re-count to the new value; it cross-fades over 200ms while the block appears, so the eye sees a substitution accompanied by an explanation. `MotionBudget.still`: both instant, and the block simply appears. Tapping the block opens the full scoring provenance.
items.modes: Night: `well` #141D27, ink-3 at 6.41:1 on it. Day: #E2DBCC, ink-3 at 4.52:1 — the binding Day case, and it passes. Veld: white with a 2px #1B2632 border, all three lines at 17/600 minimum, the hollow triangle at 10dp with a 2px stroke, and "Provisional" replaced by the fuller "Not final yet", because outdoors there is no tap-to-learn.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(liveRegion: true)` on the block, announcing once: "Your score changed. Final 71. You saw 84 on your phone. Two sections' photos arrived after scoring." The provisional marker announces as part of the figure's value — "84, provisional" — so the dotted underline is never the only carrier. At 2.0× the three lines wrap freely and the block grows. Non-colour: dotted versus solid, hollow versus filled glyph, three sentences.
items.amber: None. This is a moment of doubt about a number, and the law is explicit that amber never says how much to trust something.
items.screenshot: Under a big number with a fine dotted line beneath it, a sunken dark slab with a faint outline: Final and 71 in bright monospace, below it On your phone and 84 in grey monospace with a small hollow triangle pointing down between them, and a grey sentence, Two sections' photos arrived after scoring.

items.name: TableTwin
items.purpose: The numbers behind every visual — the accessibility path, the export path, and the answer to 'analysts who want a spreadsheet'.
items.anatomy:
Opened by the "See the numbers" control that every chart and every cluster carries, and by a plain tap on any TrendChart. A bottom sheet: radius 14 top, `surface` #1B2632, 1px `edge-structure` at 3.00:1, a 40×4dp Oatmeal@40% grabber, scrim `ground`@72%, NO blur (there is zero `BackdropFilter` in the application).

Header: the visual's own title at title.l 20/600, the window and the source at meta 12 ink-3, and the full untruncated series names the legend had to ellipsis.

Body: a two- or three-column table. Row height 44dp (Field 48, Veld 64), divided by 1px hairlines. Column 1 the label at body 15/400 ink-1, wrapping to 2 lines, never truncated — this is where a full outlet name lives. Columns 2+ the figures, right-aligned, mono, FULL PRECISION AND NEVER COMPACTED, with their units. A delta column when the visual had deltas, using the same Delta component at its inline size, including its suppression rules — a delta the chart refused to draw is not resurrected here.

Footer: `Copy all` and `Export CSV` as ghost buttons at 44dp, and the provenance line — the query in `mono.ident` 13/500 JetBrains Mono, exactly the role machine identifiers are for.

Horizontal overflow: the table scrolls horizontally inside its own region; the sheet body never scrolls sideways.
items.states: Normal. Long (>50 rows) → virtualised with a sticky header row. Empty → the same left-aligned empty state the visual showed, so the two never disagree. Single row → rendered as a row, not as a special case. Dropped rows → rows the visual excluded (null values, beyond the cap) are INCLUDED here and marked "not ranked" in a trailing meta column; the twin is the complete set by definition. Error → the sheet opens with the error and a retry rather than not opening, because a control that does nothing is worse than one that explains. Offline → cached rows with the held chip in its header. Copying → a 1200ms toast and text that is locale-correct, uncompacted and tab-separated.
items.behaviour: Opens over 320ms. Dismissed by drag, scrim tap or back. The control that opens it is never hidden behind an overflow menu — it is a first-class sibling of the chart. Export builds on a background isolate through the SAME TiqNumber, so a figure cannot be formatted one way on screen and another in the PDF. `MotionBudget.still`: opens without the slide.
items.modes: Night `surface`. Day #FAF7F2 with sh3. Veld: not a sheet at all but a full-screen white route with a 2px-bordered header and 64dp rows, because a sheet with a scrim is a fiddly dismissal target in the sun.
items.accessibility: This is the surface's primary accessibility contract: every chart in the product is reachable as a table, and the table is a real semantics tree with row and column headers, not a `CustomPaint`. Announced as "Table, 8 rows, 3 columns". Focus moves into the sheet on open and returns to the control on close. At 2.0× the label column takes its two lines, rows grow, and the figure columns scroll horizontally rather than shrinking. Non-colour: it is a table.
items.amber: None. The twin is a document.
items.screenshot: A dark sheet risen from the bottom with a small grabber, a title, and a plain table: outlet names down the left in off-white, percentages right-aligned in monospace, small coloured triangles and signed numbers in a third column, hairlines between every row, and at the foot two quiet buttons and a line of monospace showing the query that produced it.

items.name: DataSkeleton
items.purpose: What every figure and visual looks like while it is loading — geometry without shimmer, and without the amber that would claim it is live.
items.anatomy:
Static blocks at `well` fill (Night #141D27, Day #E2DBCC), radius 6, in the EXACT geometry of the content they stand in for: a figure block at the rendered width of a representative figure for that role, measured the same way FigureSlot measures; a label block at 60% of the label's line width; a chart's full frame — gridlines, axes, tick labels — at full value with one block in the plot area.

One 1px `edge-control` rule wherever the real hairline will be, so the layout does not shift by a pixel when data lands.

After 600ms of waiting, ONE Oatmeal #C9C1B1 2dp rule travels the top edge of the whole loading region at 1400ms linear, repeating. Not amber — a skeleton is loading, not live, and pulsing amber on a placeholder would tell a manager a placeholder is live data. One rule per region, never one per block.
items.states: Under 600ms → static blocks, no rule; most loads finish here and a rule that appears and vanishes is worse than none. Over 600ms → the travelling rule. Over 8s → the rule stops and a line appears: "Still fetching — this window is large" at meta ink-3, with a ghost `Cancel`. Failed → the error state replaces it; a skeleton never simply persists. Partially loaded → what arrived renders fully, what has not keeps its blocks, and the travelling rule covers only the still-loading region. Refresh (data already on screen) → NO skeleton at all; the existing figures stay and the cluster footer shows a 2dp indeterminate rule. Replacing a skeleton with a no-data state → a 200ms cross-fade, so an em dash does not appear to be a loaded value.
items.behaviour: The travelling rule is one of three subscribers to the application's single `Ticker`, and it unsubscribes when `MotionBudget.still` turns true, so a still screen schedules no frames. Never inside a `ListView.builder` row with a gradient — the rule is a `ColoredBox` translated by an `Animation`, not a shader.
items.modes: Night blocks #141D27, rule #C9C1B1 at 9.51:1 on them. Day blocks #E2DBCC, rule #4A4437 at 7.01:1. Veld: NO skeleton at all — the word "Loading" in body.strong 17/600 veld-ink, left-aligned at the gutter, and nothing else. Grey blocks on white in the sun are invisible, and an agent needs a word.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(label: 'Loading figures', liveRegion: true)` announced once on entry and once on completion ("Four figures loaded"), never per block and never per frame. The blocks are `ExcludeSemantics`. At 2.0× blocks scale with their role so the geometry promise holds. Non-colour: the word and the announcement, not the shimmer.
items.amber: None, and this is a rule with a history: an earlier draft put a pulsing amber on the skeleton, which under the system's own "breathing amber means live" law told the user a placeholder was live data.
items.screenshot: A panel with the right shape but no content: dull sunken rectangles where numbers will be, shorter ones where labels will be, faint rules dividing them, and a thin oatmeal line sliding slowly across the panel's top edge.

items.name: DataEmpty
items.purpose: A visual with nothing to draw — distinguished, always, from a visual that failed and from a visual full of zeros.
items.anatomy:
LEFT-ALIGNED, never centred. Inside a panel: a 40dp 2px-stroke line drawing in `edge-control` (6.02:1 on the Night ground, 4.69:1 on Palladian) — a shelf outline, not an icon-font glyph, not an emoji — s4 16dp, a headline at title.m 16/600 ink-1, s2 8dp, one body 15/400 ink-2 line naming what would produce data, s4 16dp, one ghost secondary button at 44dp (Field 48, Veld 56).

Standing alone on a screen: the same structure at display 40 for the headline and a 64dp drawing.

The body line names the NEXT PHYSICAL ACTION where one exists, not the absence: "No visits to Gauteng North in week 38. Widen the window, or check the beat plan." — never "No data available."
items.states: Empty window (nothing happened). Empty filter (data exists, the filter excludes it) → different headline, and the button is `Clear filter`. Empty because unauthorised (territory not the viewer's) → different headline, no button, one line naming who to ask; never the same treatment as an absence, because "you can't see this" and "this didn't happen" are opposite facts. Empty because the metric is not configured for this client → "This client does not track share of shelf", no button. Empty AND offline → the empty state plus the held chip; an empty cached window may simply be a window that never synced, and the chip says so. All-zero (NOT empty) → never this state; zeros render as zeros with a meta line. Empty after a refresh that used to have data → the empty state plus "There were 14 visits here last week", because a window going from 14 to 0 is itself the finding.
items.behaviour: Appears with a 200ms enter after any skeleton cross-fades out. The button is the only interactive element and is a real action, never "Retry" — retry belongs to the error state. No motion of its own, no animated illustration.
items.modes: Night: drawing `edge-control` #7C93AC, headline ink-1 at 15.77:1, body ink-2 at 10.67:1. Day: #6E6657 drawing, ink-1 at 12.67:1. Veld: drawing at 3px #1B2632, headline 18/600, body 17/600, button 56dp — and Veld drops the drawing entirely below 400dp of height, keeping the words.
items.accessibility: `Semantics(label: <headline>, hint: <body line>)` on a container; the drawing is `ExcludeSemantics`. Announced on arrival as a live region so a screen-reader user is not left listening to silence after a load. Button ≥44/48/56dp with a real label, never an icon alone. At 2.0× everything wraps and the drawing does not scale.
items.amber: None. An empty state is the classic place a brand colour gets sprinkled to cheer it up, and cheering up an absence is exactly the dishonesty this layer exists to avoid.
items.screenshot: Hung off the left gutter: a simple two-stroke line drawing of an empty shelf, then in off-white, No visits in week 38, then in grey, Widen the window, or check the beat plan, then a quiet outlined button reading Widen to 30 days.

items.name: DataError and stale
items.purpose: Two failures the product must never conflate: we could not fetch this, and this is older than you think.
items.anatomy:
ERROR, inside a cluster or a chart: the frame and every label render normally; figures become em dashes; ONE line appears in the region's footer at body 15/400 ink-2 with a 7dp half-filled `bad` triangle: "Couldn't load these figures." plus a meta line with the reason when the client has one ("No connection" / "Timed out" / "Server error 502"), and ONE ghost `Retry` at 44dp. One retry per region, never per tile — four retry buttons in a cluster is an apology, not an affordance.

The error line never turns the panel red, never takes a `bad` fill, and never replaces the panel's outline with a `bad` one. Severity's critical level — a solid `bad-solid` block with a 3dp left bar — is reserved for what the DATA says, not for what the network did.

STALE / OFFLINE: not an error at all. Figures render from cache at full ink. The region's footer carries the held chip: Oatmeal ink on the `well` at 9.51:1 (Day #4A4437 on #E2DBCC at 7.01:1), 1px `edge-control`, radius 6, 44dp, a 7dp filled SQUARE glyph, "Held · as at 14:02". Warm, neutral, deliberately not a severity, because towers go down with the grid and cached figures are a normal Tuesday.

STALE BEYOND A THRESHOLD (declared per metric; default 24h): the chip gains the age in words — "Held · yesterday 14:02" — and each figure gains a meta line "as at yesterday". Never a red badge, never a strikethrough, never a dimmed figure.
items.states: Network error. Server error (reason shown). Parse error — the payload arrived but could not be read: the tiles that parsed render, the footer reads "2 of 4 figures couldn't be read", and the failure is logged, not surfaced as a stack. Partial error. Auth expired → not this state; a route-level interstitial, because retrying will never work. Retrying → the `Retry` button takes three 6dp Oatmeal dots on a 600ms travel, never a spinner, and under `MotionBudget.still` the word "Retrying…". Retry failed twice → the reason gains "Still failing — this may be us" and a `Report` ghost. Stale. Stale and failing to refresh → BOTH: cached figures at full ink, the held chip, AND the error line; two independent facts, and collapsing them hides one. Recovered → figures cross-fade 200ms and re-count from their previous values, and the footer clears.
items.behaviour: Retry re-fetches the whole region, not one tile. Automatic retry happens at most twice, with 2s and 8s backoff, silently — a visible countdown is anxiety. The held chip is tappable and opens the sync sheet showing what is queued and how large it is; ticket #378's live outbox row lives there, not here.

items.name: AmberLedger
items.purpose: Makes the amber law countable and enforceable by a test that can actually see amber — rewritten, because the first version's enforcement could not be implemented and its capacities broke the law they existed to keep.
items.anatomy:
**CAPACITY — THE LAW IS TWO, AND CHROME COUNTS.** The first draft declared the answer route at 3 content objects plus a chrome underbar — four — while its own principles line said two, and the direction spec says "3 in content, plus the chrome underbar" on that screen and "2 objects" on the dashboard, counting chrome in one place and not the other. Three documents, three numbers. Resolved here, one way, in writing: **at most two amber objects on any screen, and the chrome underbar is one of them.**

The consequence is severe and deliberate. Amber appears in the data layer of this product EXACTLY ONCE: the single focus bar, or the single series, on the answered Ask TradeIQ route. Everywhere else — the dashboard, every agent screen, every Day and Veld screen — every chart renders in ink-1, which measures higher (9.43:1 versus 6.37:1 on the Night track) and is already how the Day chart draws. That is the torch: one light, in one place, on the one screen that exists to answer one question.

**PHASES, NOT FRAMES, NOT VIEWPORTS.** The answer route has two composition phases that are never on screen together: WORKING (the step rail runs) and ANSWERED (the steps collapse to completed Oatmeal dots and the visuals land). Capacity is declared per phase, both statically known at route construction:
- Working: nav underbar (chrome) + the running-step pulse = 2.
- Answered: nav underbar (chrome) + ONE content emitter = 2.
The direction's one semantic amber — the motion-coded live pulse — therefore survives intact rather than being deleted for a budget it never actually shared. Phase is not viewport: a visual that scrolls out of view does NOT release its slot, because a slot that released on scroll would make amber blink in and out under the reader's thumb.
- Manager dashboard: plate strip light + nav underbar = 2. Data layer: 0.
- Agent Day/Veld: the primary commit action = 1.
- Agent Night with tabs: commit action rim + nav underbar = 2. Data layer: 0.
- Inside a visit (no tabs): commit action rim = 1, and the second is deliberately unspent — a capture screen with a spare torch is a capture screen that stays dark.

PRIORITIES within the answered phase are theme constants, not arguments: ranked-bar focus p0, trend series p1, diverging axis p0 (it displaces the focus row in its own list, since a diverging chart without a visible zero is unreadable). Two engineers cannot both claim p0 because neither writes the number.

**RESOLUTION IS STATIC.** The first draft had children "request a slot at build" from an `InheritedWidget` — but an inherited payload is fixed for the frame, so a ledger that notices it is over capacity can only correct on the next frame, and the manager watches amber appear on frame 1 and vanish on frame 2. On a 2 GB Android under memory pressure that is a visible blink on every answer. Since capacities are route constants and priorities are theme constants, grants are fully determinable before the first build: the route resolves them into a `const Set<AmberSlot>` at construction and passes it down as immutable data. The `InheritedWidget` only reads. The runtime request/deny machinery and the release-mode silent-demotion path are both deleted.

**RELEASED SLOTS ARE RETIRED, NOT REASSIGNED.** When `MotionBudget.still` degrades the live pulse to a filled square plus the word "Live", its slot reduces the phase's effective capacity rather than returning to the pool. The first draft promoted a denied focus bar in its place, which meant a manager at 9% battery who asked the phone to use less power was rewarded with the largest, brightest, most expensive amber region in the data layer appearing on screen. Degradation may only ever remove amber.

**ENFORCEMENT IS AT THE PIXEL.** The first draft's test claimed to walk the render tree counting `Color` instances and grouping contiguous ones. It cannot be written: the trend series, the focus bloom, the origin marker and every hatch are `Paint` objects constructed inside `paint()`, invisible to any `Element` or `RenderObject` traversal, and Flutter exposes no canvas interception; "contiguous" is a property of pixels, not of a tree. An engineer would have written it in sprint one, watched it pass trivially because every amber in the data layer is inside a `CustomPaint`, marked it green, and the law would have been unenforced from the day it landed. Replaced by, in about sixty lines:
1. Render each route's golden at each phase in all three skins via `tester.binding.renderView.toImage()`.
2. Connected-component label every pixel within a ΔE threshold of any flame token, 8-connected, discarding components under 12px².
3. Fail above the phase's declared capacity, printing the component count and bounding boxes.
4. A companion lint forbids any reference to `TiqSkin.flame*` outside a hand-registered allowlist of emitter widgets, so a new emitter cannot appear without someone editing the ledger in the same commit.

**ONE FLAME TOKEN SHIPS.** `flame-500`, `flame-700` and `flame-900` appeared nowhere in this surface except inside the lint's own scan list, and `flame-300` existed for an export that has no amber in it — tokens with no call site are permission to use them, and an engineer picking the middle one of four ships a second amber the golden may not catch. `TiqSkin` carries `flame-600` #FFB162 and nothing else; the paper-safe amber, if the PDF ever needs one, is `flame-print` in the PDF theme where no widget can reach it. The lint keeps scanning for all four names so a resurrected token still fails the build.
items.states: Granted → the visual emits. Denied → the fallback: ink-1 fill plus marker plus weight for a focus bar; ink-1 2dp stroke for a series; a pulsing `lifted` dot plus the word "Live" for a live figure. Capacity-0 route → nothing requests and the fallback is the ONLY rendering, which is why the fallback must be first-class rather than a degradation — and on the revised budget it is what ships nearly everywhere. Day or Veld → the data layer's capacity is 0 by construction and the ledger is not consulted. Over-declaration in debug → an assertion at route construction naming the route, the phase and the offending slot, before a frame is built. Over-declaration in CI → the pixel golden fails with bounding boxes.
items.behaviour: Resolved once, at route construction, never per frame and never per scroll. The live-pulse subscriber shares the application's single 3200ms `Ticker` and unsubscribes when `MotionBudget.still` turns true, retiring its slot as it goes.
items.modes: Night: the ledger has capacity and is consulted. Day: data-layer capacity 0; the one amber block is the route's registered primary commit action. Veld: identical to Day, and the amber block is the only amber on the screen — never a line, never an icon, never a border, never a word (1.79:1 on white).
items.accessibility: Invisible to the user by design, and that is the point: nothing depends on whether a slot was granted, because every amber channel has a non-amber partner — shape, weight, dash, marker or word — present either way. A screen reader's experience is byte-identical with and without amber.
items.amber: It is the amber accountant. It emits none itself.
items.screenshot: Not a visual. Its test output is: `answer_route[answered] · night: 2/2 amber components — nav_underbar(chrome, 412px²), ranked_bar_focus(p0, 2 180px²). PASS.` and, on a violation, `dashboard_route · night: 7/2 amber components — plate_strip, nav_underbar, and 5 components of 9–14px² at x∈[288,352] (sparkline dots). FAIL.`

items.name: HatchPaint and stripe registry
items.purpose: One registry of every non-solid fill in the product, so two different meanings can never be given the same stripe.
items.anatomy:
Four patterns, and only four. Each is drawn as LINES IN A `CustomPainter` inside an existing draw call; the hard-stop repeating `LinearGradient` form is permitted only on a non-scrolling child. Never a shader, never a `saveLayer`, never `ImageFiltered`.

1. NOT MEASURED — 45° FALLING (↘), 1.2dp lines at a 5dp period, `edge-control` on the track colour (3.60:1 Night, 4.12:1 Day). Always spans the full track. Meaning: no measurement exists.
2. NEGATIVE DIVERGING — 45° RISING (↗), 3dp stripes at a 6dp period, `bad` on the track colour (4.65:1 Night, 6.60:1 Day). Proportional to the value. Meaning: a magnitude below zero.
3. LOW SAMPLE — not a hatch but an OUTLINE: the mark drawn as a 1.5dp stroke of its normal fill colour with no fill. Meaning: the number is weak.
4. PROVISIONAL — the same outline as (3) plus a 2dp dotted underline on the accompanying figure. Meaning: not final.

The registry is a Dart enum with a doc comment and a golden per member. A fifth pattern requires deleting one — the constraint is the mechanism, because four distinguishable fills is roughly the limit of what survives greyscale, both common dichromacies, a printed PDF and a 6-bit LCD at 40% backlight. **The registry's first test was its own author**: the BandScale wanted hatch/dotted/solid for its three bands, which would have given one material two meanings on a single screen, and the BandScale was redesigned to use threshold marks instead. A cap honoured only against other people is not a cap.

**MINIMUM SIZE IS A HARD RULE, NOT A GUIDELINE.** No pattern on a mark under 4dp, and no pattern inside a glyph — a 5dp period inside a 20dp disc is five stripes that render as a flat mid-grey, which is why ticket #375's "can't confirm" is a barred ring and not a hatched one. Below 4dp the mark takes the outline form.

Stripe geometry NEVER scales with text: these are graphics. It DOES change per skin: Veld coarsens every period by 60% (5→8dp, 6→10dp) and thickens every line to 2px, because a fine stripe at arm's length in glare is a flat grey.
items.states: Each pattern's own states are specified at its owning component. Registry-level: two patterns in one object → forbidden, asserted by a test. A pattern on a mark under 4dp or inside a glyph → forbidden, asserted by a test that measures the painted rect. A pattern in a `ListView.builder` row → the painter form only; the gradient form is counted against the 12-gradients-per-screen budget and the diverging ranked list is that budget's named worst case and its named test. Print/PDF export → all four survive unchanged; this is the reason they exist.
items.behaviour: Never animates. A growing hatched bar animates its LENGTH with the stripes fixed in world space so they do not appear to travel — a moving stripe reads as a progress indicator. The painter anchors the phase to the bar's origin, not to its current width.
items.modes: Night: not-measured #7C93AC on #2C3B4D; negative #FF7D8C on #2C3B4D. Day: #6E6657 on #E2DBCC; #8C1B2C on #E2DBCC. Veld: both in #1B2632 on white at the coarsened periods, distinguished from each other by DIRECTION alone — which is sufficient, because direction is a shape and Veld's whole argument is that shape beats hue outdoors.
items.accessibility: A pattern never carries meaning alone: each of the four is paired with a mandatory word — "not measured", the signed value, "from 3 visits", "provisional" — in the owning component's semantics. The patterns are `ExcludeSemantics`. At 2.0× unchanged. This registry is precisely the system's answer to "colour is never the only signal".
items.amber: None. No amber is ever hatched, striped, dotted or outlined — amber is emitted light and light has no texture. An amber focus bar is always a solid fill with a gradient bloom, which is why the diverging-negative focus row falls back to an amber outline plus bloom rather than an amber hatch, and why on the revised budget it usually falls back to ink-1 instead.
items.screenshot: A specimen sheet: four short bars side by side on dark ground — one filled corner to corner with pale diagonals falling right, one two-thirds filled with red diagonals rising right, one drawn as a thin hollow outline, one the same outline with a dotted line beneath it — each labelled beneath in small grey caps.

openQuestions:
THE AMBER BUDGET IS NOW STRICTER THAN THE DIRECTION SPEC, AND THE OWNER HAS TO SEE THAT. The spec's screens field budgets the Ask TradeIQ answer at "3 in content, plus the chrome underbar" — four amber regions. The owner's law says two, counted. My first draft encoded the spec's number and then wrote "at most two emitters" in its own principles line, contradicting itself in the same document. Resolved one way: two per screen, chrome counted, phases declared separately so the working-step pulse (the direction's one semantic, motion-coded amber) keeps its slot in a phase where nothing else is on screen. The consequence is that amber appears in the data layer of this entire product exactly once — the single focus bar, or the single series, on the answered answer route — and every chart on the dashboard, on every agent screen, and in Day and Veld renders in ink-1 at higher contrast. I believe this is the direction's thesis taken seriously rather than decorated. But it is a smaller, harder product than the spec's screen budgets describe, and it is a decision the owner must make rather than discover at goldens.

TYPEFACE COLLISION, AND IT IS STILL LOAD-BEARING. The spec's typography field names Archivo Variable for UI, figures and display, with JetBrains Mono surviving only for machine identifiers, and it builds the hero fitting rule on Archivo's proportional advance and a wdth 88–112 axis. The owner's decision list names Onest for prose and JetBrains Mono for EVERY figure in a data role. I built on the owner's decision as the later, not-to-be-reopened instruction, and three things in the spec became wrong: (a) the hero fitting rule is measured, not glyph-counted, because a 0.600 em advance under a non-linear TextScaler makes glyph count unsafe; (b) the −2.5%/−1.5%/−1.0% tracking on figure roles is deleted, since negative tracking collapses monospace cells; (c) neither Onest nor JetBrains Mono has a wdth axis, so the spec's "opt-in condensation on two or three measured labels" insurance is gone and wrapping is the only overflow mechanism. Someone must still confirm the owner wants mono figures at 72dp — a hero in JetBrains Mono Bold reads as a fuel gauge, which may be exactly right for this product or exactly wrong, and it is a five-minute specimen test rather than an argument.

THE AMBER TARGET TICK — I OVERRODE THE DIRECTION, AND MY FIRST REASON WAS WRONG. The spec specifies a 2px #FFB162 tick breaking the meter's track. I made every tick ink-1. My first draft justified it with "four amber ticks in a 2×2 cluster", and there is no 2×2 cluster on a phone — 360dp minus gutters and panel padding is 288dp of inner width, below the grid's own threshold, so that argument described a tablet. The real reason survives and is stronger: the ledger counts per route, not per viewport, because a slot that released on scroll would make amber blink as a manager thumbs down the page — and a dashboard route carries up to four metered tiles plus a six-row dimension breakdown, ten ticks, on a route whose two slots are already spent on the plate's strip light and the nav underbar. If the owner wants the amber tick back, the only consistent way is one tick per route, on the focus metric only, granted through the ledger — which on the dashboard means displacing the strip light or the underbar.

THE WIRE SAYS 'amber' AND IT CANNOT. `ServerScorecard.ratingBand` is 'green' | 'amber' | 'red', and app_en.arb renders them as "Green" / "Amber" / "Red" (af: "Groen" / "Oranje" / "Rooi"). A system whose central law is that amber is never a severity cannot have a severity band literally named Amber. I have specified Healthy / Watch / Gap, with Watch carrying the outlined-crimson commitment level. This needs a wire migration or a client-side mapping plus six translated strings, and the client's published banding has to agree — the bands are the client's contract with their own field force, not ours to rename unilaterally.

PROVISIONAL SCORING REVERSES A DELIBERATE PRODUCT DECISION. `visit_outcome_screen.dart` and the string `outcomeNoGuess` ("Your real score — the one your manager sees — appears once this reaches the server") exist because someone decided an agent shown 74 in the shop who finds 68 in the morning will not trust the third number. Ticket #377 asks for the opposite. I have designed the reconciliation treatment and KEPT the current no-guess behaviour on the outcome screen, so the two cannot both ship by accident. My view: the reconciliation block is good enough that provisional becomes safe, PROVIDED the server, not the client, computes the provisional value and stamps it — the client's offline proxy would change for reasons the agent can never see, which is the failure the original decision was protecting against.

THREE FIELDS ARE NOT ON THE WIRE, AND ONE OF THEM IS NEW. I have specified that the server sends `decimals`, `sampleSize` and — added in this revision — `baselineSampleSize`, and that the client never invents any of them. None exists today. Without `decimals` the client guesses significant figures on money. Without `sampleSize` the low-sample state cannot fire at all. Without `baselineSampleSize` a delta can render a hard red verdict computed against a single visit in the prior window, which on a load-shedding calendar is the common case, not the edge case: twenty visits at 84% against one strike-week visit at 100% renders "−16 pts vs week 37" in full confidence and a manager reassigns an agent over it. Same migration, one more field. The thresholds I declared (n≥5 rates, n≥3 averages) are defaults to be argued with, not measured — someone with the visit distribution should set them.

THE POWER-SAVE CHANNEL IS A DELIVERABLE, NOT A FLAG. A dozen components in the first draft gated motion on "battery-saver" as though it were a MediaQuery field. Flutter has no power API: `MediaQuery.disableAnimations` comes from `AccessibilityFeatures.disableAnimations`, which on Android tracks `TRANSITION_ANIMATION_SCALE == 0`, not power saving. I have collapsed all twelve gates into one `MotionBudget.still`, whose third input is explicitly `const false` with a ticket on it until someone writes the `EventChannel` (Android `PowerManager.isPowerSaveMode` + `ACTION_POWER_SAVE_MODE_CHANGED`; iOS `NSProcessInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled` + its notification — roughly forty lines each). It needs to be scheduled or the sentence needs to come out of the design entirely. What it cannot do is stay in the prose while resolving to nothing, which is where it was.

THE GAUGE IS CUT. I specified a 96dp ScoreArc in the first draft because the brief asked for a compact score mark. It had no call site, cost a `drawArc` per instance, capped at 8 per list and silently became a Meter beyond that — so the same outlet showed a ring in a list of six and a bar in a list of nine. It is replaced by ScoreMark: a meter, a figure and a band word, the pattern the rest of this surface already uses. If the owner wanted a gauge specifically, say so now, before the painter exists.

THE CONTRAST FIGURES ARE REGENERATED, AND ONE TOKEN MOVED. Every ratio in this document now comes from a script run against the tokens rather than from memory. Three of the first draft's numbers were wrong: ink-1 on the bar track is 9.43:1 and not 11.12 (11.12 is ink-1 on `raised`, a different pair); ink-3 on the `well` is 6.41:1 and not 7.19; and the sentence claiming the ink-1 fallback out-contrasts amber compared a Day pair against a Night pair, though the claim happens to survive when measured in one mode. Two real defects fell out: `edge-structure` on `raised` is 2.63:1, so the scrub readout's outline moves to `edge-control` at 4.25:1; and `chart-neutral` #8B8271 measured exactly 3.01:1 against its track — the most-drawn graphic in the product sitting on the AA floor with 0.01 of margin. It moves to #A39887 (4.02:1), and the Day neutral moves to #5C5648 (5.29:1) because the old value was byte-identical to Day ink-3. I did not take it to 4.5:1 as asked: 4.5 is the text threshold and a bar is a graphical object at 3:1 — the defect was the absent margin, not the threshold.

WHAT I STILL CANNOT RESOLVE ALONE: whether a phone dashboard should carry four figures at all. The 2×2 grid the first draft assumed cannot render on a 360dp phone, and the horizontal tile I have designed instead saves about 160dp across four tiles — but four tiles plus a footer is still roughly 470dp, most of the fold, before a manager reaches a single ranked bar. I have written the cluster to take up to four and recommended three. Which three is a product question about what a manager acts on before breakfast, and nobody in this document knows the answer.
principles: Figures carry this product's credibility, so this layer's first duty is to refuse to lie. A zero is a measurement; a null is an absence; not-measured is a third thing with its own material and its own sentence. Nothing is inferred — direction, sentiment, precision, sample size and the baseline's sample size come from the server or are not shown. Amber is emitted light, and this layer holds exactly one emitter in the entire product: the single bar or series the answer's sentence is about, counted at the pixel by a golden test, with chrome counted too. Every hue-coded distinction carries a second channel: shape, weight, dash, hatch or word. Every chart has a table twin. Figures are monospace, tabular, measured to fit with their affixes, and never pinned against text scaling. Every promise here is one the code can keep.
